new_roles.description:
**What To Expect**
Tesla is seeking a highly motivated Sr. Staff Manufacturing Engineer to build and lead a team of engineers focused on high-volume production launches. This role will drive the development of scalable manufacturing systems while collaborating with cross-functional teams to optimize product designs for manufacturability, accelerate assembly processes, and implement automation solutions. In this fast-paced, demanding environment, you’ll play a pivotal role in scaling Tesla’s SI robotics initiatives while advancing our mission to achieve sustainable abundance through innovative manufacturing practices.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Lead Manufacturing Engineering Team: Build, mentor, and scale high-performing teams to design and deploy high-volume production systems, ensuring alignment with Tesla’s speed and quality objectives
- Collaborate with Equipment Suppliers: Partner with internal and external suppliers to engineer, install, and validate production equipment, accelerating line ramp-up to meet volume targets
- Validate Requirements and Constraints: Use first principles analysis to rigorously assess product and process requirements, eliminating ambiguity and ensuring all elements are purpose-driven and essential
- Optimize Production Processes: Identify and remove non-value-added steps in workflows, prioritizing functional simplicity before pursuing automation or advanced optimization
- Improve Cycle Time: Analyze production bottlenecks and implement solutions to increase process speed, throughput, and overall line efficiency
- Deploy Automation Solutions: Strategically integrate automation as a final step after process simplification, ensuring systems are robust, high-speed, and scalable
- Ensure Seamless Operational Transitions: Coordinate with operations teams during ramp-up phases, delivering detailed documentation and training to sustain engineering teams for long-term success
**What You'll Bring**- First Principles Thinking: A rigorous mindset focused on breaking down complex problems to their fundamental truths, enabling innovative solutions to manufacturing challenges
- Proficiency in CAD tools (Catia and AutoCAD preferred) for designing and optimizing production systems
- Deep knowledge of mechanical assembly techniques (pressing, fastening, harnessing, etc.) and electrical integration, including quality control matrices, testing protocols, and troubleshooting methodologies
- Familiarity with torque tools, automation equipment, control systems, and communication protocols (e.g., PLC, HMI, SCADA)
- Production Transition Experience: Demonstrated success in scaling products from prototype to high-volume production, ensuring seamless handover to sustaining teams
- Resilience & Adaptability: Ability to thrive in high-pressure environments while managing competing priorities and tight deadlines
- Communication & Organization: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, paired with meticulous attention to detail and a highly organized approach to documentation and process handover
- Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical or Electrical engineering, or equivalent experience
**Benefits**
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
 
- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
- Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
- Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
- Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
- Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
- Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
- Tesla Babies program
- Commuter benefits
- Employee discounts and perks program
- Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
Expected Compensation
 
 
$156,000 - $276,000/annual salary + cash and stock awards + benefits
 
 
Pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

new_roles.title: Sr Director - Advanced Manufacturing Engineer - NPI
new_roles.description:
**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
 
 
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
This position is incentive eligible.
 
 
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/
 
 
**POSTING TIMELINE**
The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.
 
 
Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At
**Honeywell Aerospace**
(NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.
 
 
Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.
 
 
Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.
 
 
Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.
 
 
Honeywell Aerospace Products And Services Are Found On Aircraft Across Commercial Aviation, Defense And Space. We Operate Through Three Business Areas
 
 
Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft
 
 
Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying
 
 
Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board
 
 
With approximately 58,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, we are also advancing systems for autonomous and supersonic platforms — bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. Explore our businesses: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com
 
 
Join Honeywell Aerospace! Our aerospace innovations bring people together, make the world safer and more secure, and help humankind reach for the stars. Now we’re shaping aviation’s future with sustainable aviation fuels, smarter cockpits, ultra-efficient engines, smart airports, flying taxis and much more.

new_roles.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
new_roles.description:
Join Reynolds Consumer Products…and Drive Your Career across a world of opportunities!
 
 
We currently have an opportunity for a
**Continuous Improvement Director**
at our
**Lake Forest Corporate Headquarters**
plant in
**Lake Forest, IL**
. This position will support our Malvern, AK, Louisville, KY, Bellwood, VA, and Wheeling plants with up to 75% travel. This position could also be located at our Malvern, AK, or Louisville, KY locations.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
The
**Continuous Improvement Director**
will be responsible for driving continuous improvement and demonstrating maximum efficiency and delivery productivity for the entire Business Unit (BU) with disciplined process and world class measures. The Continuous Improvement Director will be a key creator of the Continuous Improvement and Digital Factory strategy for the BU, leveraging best practices across our manufacturing sites as we continue to develop our Boundless operating system across Reynolds Consumer Products (RCP). We embrace and accept individual experiences and backgrounds to achieve a diverse and inclusive workplace.
 
 
**You Will Have the Opportunity to Make Great Things Happen!**
**Strategy & Business Transformation**

* Develop plans, schedules, and budgets for tactical projects to improve existing processes; ensure cost-benefit evaluation for all assigned projects are completed to define potential financial, business and industry impacts of initiatives.
* Support the business leaders in the development of intermediate and long-term CI strategies to assure delivery of the projected CI Saving Budget.
* Create the digital manufacturing (IoT) strategy and coach plant teams on implementation and sustained performance enhancement as a result.
* Advise and influence senior leadership on business transformation topics that include organizational effectiveness, performance results, and change management in the terms of complexity and impact on the business.

**Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence**

* Manage a CI Savings Budget across the Business Unit that represents an achievable value to deliver back to the business.
* Act as the subject matter expert for the core pillars of the Boundless operating system to assure sustained results, including assisting in training and plant acclimation to the new PEPS process.
* Drive the improvement of processes and systems in the plants and implement programs that will have continuing long-term benefits.
* Continuously evaluate and measure program or initiative performance and progress against goals and serve as a change agent within the organization.
* Monitor existing processes to make sure they continue to perform at optimal levels of efficiency achieving lowered conversion costs year-over-year.
* Direct all CI activities to include Kaizen events in 5S, SMED, TPM, VSM, PDCA or equivalent, A3 Problem Solving.
* Ensure adherence to Lean Methodology, including Kaizen, 5S, Standard Work, Daily Management, Layered Audit Process and Business Plan development to eliminate waste.
* Confer with management, engineering, and other staff regarding manufacturing capabilities, production schedules, and other considerations to facilitate production process improvements.

**Leadership & Talent Development**

* Effectively lead, manage, develop, coach, and evaluate team members and associates at various levels of experience.
* Develop and deliver Lean Training at all levels of the organization while driving Operational Excellence standards.

**You Will Love It Here If…**

* You listen, learn, and evolve
* You thrive in a fast-paced environment
* You put safety first, always
* You are passionate about collaboration, teamwork, and achieving shared goals
* You believe in treating all people with respect, operating ethically, and growing a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace
* You are committed to improving our impact on local communities and creating positive experiences

**Qualifications**
**Education/Experience**
**Required**

* BA/BS degree in Business, Supply Chain or related field.
* 10+ years of related professional Manufacturing with experience in Continuous Improvement and Operations.
* 3+ years in a leadership role focused on continuous improvement or operational excellence.

**Preferred**

* MBA or other advanced degree a plus.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt strongly preferred.
* Previous experience with Automation and SAP strongly preferred.

**Knowledge/Skills/Abilities**

* Proficient in MS Office with advanced Excel Skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentation skills and the ability to communicate and influence at all levels within the organization.
* Self-directed with the ability to work in a fast-paced environment with multiple accountabilities and multiple internal customers.
* Strong analytical skills as well as organizational skills with high attention to detail.
* Solid project management capabilities with the ability to organize and manage multiple projects simultaneously from origin through execution.
* Ability to work a flexible schedule during key business deadlines.
* Must be team oriented with the ability to work on high collaboration and performance teams.

**Competencies**

* Results Driven – Ability to focus on organizational growth, financial performance and achieving results.
* Critical Decision Maker – Clear, critical thinker that engages in thoughtful, data-driven decisions and has the ability to summarize and draw appropriate conclusions from complex data.
* Strategic Orientation – Ability to balance short-term goals with long-term organizational and functional strategic priorities.
* Innovative Thinking – A forward thinker who offers new, creative and often unconventional thoughts, opinions and methods for solution generation and problem solving.
* People Leadership – Ability to develop employees through coaching and feedback and holds team members accountable through modeling appropriate behavior.
* Compelling Communication – Effective written and verbal communicator that clearly and succinctly conveys information across all levels.

Want to know more? Check out our website or connect with us on LinkedIn!
 
 
**Apply today to join a fast-growing innovative company!**
Not a good fit but know someone who is? Please refer them!
 
 
**No unsolicited recruiter or agency inquiries, please.**
RCP affords equal employment opportunities to applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, disability status, sex, marital status, protected veteran status, pregnancy, national origin, genetics, genetic information, parental status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. RCP conforms to the spirit as well as to the letter of all applicable laws and regulations.
 
 
**Posted Salary Range**
USD $144,100.00 - USD $214,350.00 /A
 
 
**Bonus Eligibility**
Role is eligible for 25% annual incentive provided the business meets financial goals and the individual meets their performance goals, subject to plan administration guidelines.

new_roles.title: Quality/Risk Director
new_roles.description:
**Quality/Risk Director Career Opportunity**

**Highly regarded and valued for your Quality/Risk Director expertise** 
Are you seeking a career that not only utilizes your skills but also aligns with your personal values, providing a profound sense of belonging and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in patients' lives? Look no further than Encompass Health, the nation's leader in in-patient rehabilitation care. As a Quality/Risk Director, you will oversee a hospital-wide quality management program, collaborating with various stakeholders to monitor and enhance the quality of patient care services. Join a team that values collaboration, support, and inclusivity, and embark on a rewarding career close to home and close to your heart, complete with access to cutting-edge equipment and technology and a comprehensive benefits package from day one.

**A Glimpse into Our World** 
At Encompass Health, you'll experience the difference the moment you become a part of our team. Being at Encompass Health means aligning with a rapidly growing national inpatient rehabilitation leader. We take pride in the growth opportunities we offer and how our team unites for the greater good of our patients. Our achievements include being named one of the "World's Most Admired Companies" and receiving the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® Award, among other accolades, which is nothing short of amazing.

**Starting Perks and Benefits** 
At Encompass Health, we are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive, and caring environment where you can thrive. From **day one,** you will have access to:

* Affordable medical, dental, and vision plans for both full-time and part-time employees and their families.
* Generous paid time off that accrues over time.
* Opportunities for tuition reimbursement and continuing education.
* Company-matching 401(k) and employee stock purchase plans.
* Flexible spending and health savings accounts.
* A vibrant community of individuals passionate about the work they do!

**Become the Quality/Risk Director you've always aspired to be**

* Ensure compliance with regulatory agencies, accrediting bodies, corporate and hospital policies, and procedures. Develop, implement, and maintain quality assessment and improvement programs.
* Assess compliance with federal, state, and industry regulatory and accreditation standards, facilitating processes to remediate and/or maintain compliance. Provide organizational education related to regulations and standards and coordinate local, state, federal, and accreditation surveys.
* Use a variety of applications (including, but not limited to, PatCom, UDS, ORYX, and Press Ganey) to identify improvement opportunities, generate reports, research issues, identify resources, and access external databases.
* Ensure the update and maintenance of hospital plans, including the Provision of Care/Scope of Services, Leadership, Information Management, Utilization Review, Infection Control, and Patient Safety plans. Oversee risk management activities, including completion of incident reports, notice of potential claims, corrective action planning, and incident reporting to the Corporate Risk Manager.
* Coordinate the review, development, and implementation of hospital policies.
* .Communicate and collaborate with other departments to coordinate care and promptly resolve patient concerns or complaints.
* Celebrate the accomplishments and successes of our dedicated employees along the way.

**Qualifications**

* A bachelor's degree in healthcare or a related field is preferred.
* License or Certification as required by state regulations.
* Experience in Quality and/or Risk Management, including primary responsibility for performance improvement activities, regulatory compliance, conflict resolution, leadership, and risk management activities.

**The Encompass Health Way**

We proudly set the standard in care by leading with empathy, doing what's right, focusing on the positive, and standing stronger together. Encompass Health is a trusted leader in post-acute care with over 150 nationwide locations and a team of 36,000 exceptional individuals and growing!

At Encompass Health, we celebrate and welcome diversity in our inclusive culture. We provide equal employment opportunities regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin, color, creed, age, mental or physical disability, or any other protected classification.

new_roles.title: Senior Director., Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global
new_roles.description:
Req ID: 11315

**Working Location: District Columbia, Washington; Massachusetts, Westborough; Pennsylvania, Center Valley**

**Workplace Flexibility: Remote**

 

***For more than 100 years, Olympus has focused on making people’s lives healthier, safer and more fulfilling.***

Every day, we live by our philosophy, True to Life, by advancing medical technologies and elevating the standard of patient care so people everywhere can fulfill their desires, dreams, and lives.

Our five Core Values empower us to achieve Our Purpose:

**Patient Focus, Integrity, Innovation, Impact and Empathy.**

 

Learn more about Life at Olympus: https://www.olympusamerica.com/careers.

**Job Description**
-------------------

Senior Director, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global, reports to the VP, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global, and serves as a strategic legal partner to the Company's global Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and Medical Safety organizations. This role provides expert legal counsel on the full spectrum of medical device regulatory, quality, compliance, enforcement, and commercialization matters across the product lifecycle, including emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), software as a medical device (SaMD), digital health, and connected medical devices products.

Senior Director, Regulatory & Quality Counsel, Global will independently manage significant legal projects, advise leadership on complex regulatory risks, support interactions with FDA and global health authorities, lead legal support for regulatory inspections and enforcement actions, and provide strategic guidance on remediation programs, product development, commercialization, and global compliance initiatives. The role also provides leadership and oversight to other attorneys supporting the Global QARA organization.

This role covers multiple jurisdictions across the Americas, as well as other key business centers located in Japan, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, China, Asia Pacific.

**Job Duties**
--------------

* Strategic QARA Legal Support
 
 + Act as a strategic legal partner to Global Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs teams and business clients, providing practical, risk-based legal advice on regulatory, quality, compliance, and enforcement matters.
 + Provide day-to-day legal counseling to internal stakeholders on regulatory and quality matters affecting the development, manufacture, distribution, promotion, and post-market management of medical devices to support compliance with global medical device regulations.
* Global Regulatory Compliance
 
 + Counsel the business on all aspects of medical device regulation throughout the product lifecycle, including research and development, clinical activities, regulatory submissions, commercialization, post-market surveillance, quality systems compliance, and lifecycle management.
 + Assist business teams in obtaining FDA and other global regulatory clearances, approvals, registrations, licenses, and certifications necessary to market medical device products.
 + Support compliance with post-market regulatory requirements, including reporting obligations, field actions, recalls, and corrective actions.
 + Draft, review, and provide legal guidance regarding policies, procedures, quality system documentation, guidance documents, product manuals, training materials, and governance documents.
* Inspections, Enforcement, and Remediation
 
 + Advise the business regarding FDA inspections and inspections conducted by global regulatory authorities, including Notified Bodies, Health Canada, MHRA, PMDA, TGA, ANVISA, and other competent authorities.
 + Support inspection readiness activities, inspection management, inspector interactions, document production, escalation processes, and post-inspection response strategies. Provide legal advice regarding inspectional observations (e.g., Form 483 observations), warning letters, import alerts, recalls, detentions and import restrictions, regulatory investigations, and other enforcement actions by FDA and global health authorities. Advise and assist in drafting responses to inspectional observations, regulatory inquiries, Warning Letters, and other enforcement communications.
 + Provide strategic legal oversight for remediation and quality-system improvement programs arising from FDA or other regulatory authority findings.
* Import and Export Compliance
 
 + Advise on FDA and global medical device import and export requirements. Provide legal support regarding import-for-export requirements, import alerts, detentions, product admissibility issues, global distribution and supply chain activities, and resolution of import restrictions and enforcement actions.

**Job Qualifications**
----------------------

**Required:**

* Minimum of 10 years of legal experience supporting FDA-regulated medical device companies.
* Combination of in-house counsel, law firm, and/or regulatory agency experience, including FDA experience.
* Significant experience advising medical device businesses on regulatory, quality, compliance, and enforcement matters.
* Demonstrated experience counseling senior leadership regarding global recalls, FDA inspections, Form 483 observations, Warning Letters, Import Alerts, and other enforcement actions.
* Experience leading or advising on complex remediation programs arising from FDA or other regulatory authority findings.
* Experience supporting inspections and interactions with FDA and global regulatory authorities.
* Experience advising on medical device import/export requirements and regulatory trade compliance issues.
* Experience managing complex cross-functional legal and compliance initiatives in a global environment.
* Deep expertise in medical device regulatory and quality law.
* Strong understanding of FDA medical device requirements and global regulatory frameworks.
* Strong understanding of enforcement trends and evolving regulatory requirements affecting digital health and AI-enabled medical devices.
* Excellent judgment and ability to provide practical, business-oriented legal advice in complex situations.
* Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, and collaboration skills.
* Proven ability to influence executive leadership and effectively manage multiple high-priority matters simultaneously.
* Ability to operate successfully in a fast-paced, highly regulated, global environment.
* Flexibility to work across global time zones, including early morning or evening calls in support of a large, global, matrixed organization.
* Travel up to 15% of time is anticipated.
 

**Preferred:**

* Experience supporting Class I, II, and III medical devices.
* Experience advising on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Software in a Medical Device (SiMD), connected medical devices, digital health platforms, mobile medical applications, remote monitoring technologies, and AI/ML-enabled medical devices.
* Experience with EU MDR, UK MDR, ISO 13485, and other global medical device regulatory frameworks.
* Experience managing external regulatory counsel and consultants.

**Why join Olympus?**

We offer a holistic employee experience supporting personal and professional well-being through meaningful work, equitable offerings, and a connected culture.

 

**Equitable Offerings you can count on:**

* Competitive salaries, annual bonus and 401(k)\* with company match
* Comprehensive medical, dental, vision coverage effective on start date
* 24/7 Employee Assistance Program
* Free live and on-demand Wellbeing Programs
* Generous Paid Vacation and Sick Time
* Paid Parental Leave and Adoption Assistance\*
* 12 Paid Holidays
* On-Site Child Daycare, Café, Fitness Center\*\*

**Connected Culture you can embrace:**

* Work-life integrated culture that supports an employee centric mindset
* Offers onsite, hybrid and field work environments
* Paid volunteering and charitable donation/match programs
* Employee Resource Groups
* Dedicated Training Resources and Learning & Development Programs
* Paid Educational Assistance

* US Only

\*\*Center Valley, PA and Westborough, MA

 

**Are you ready to be a part of our team?**

Learn more about our benefits and incentives: https://www.olympusamerica.com/careers/benefits-perks.

 

The anticipated base pay range for this full-time position is $224,401.00 - $359,041.00 / year, plus potential for annual bonus (subject to plan eligibility and other requirements). This pay range represents the National Average of the range, and may vary depending on the location of the individual.

 

Olympus considers a variety of factors when determining actual compensation for this position, including level of experience, working location, and relevant education and certifications.

 

At Olympus, we are committed to Our Purpose of making people’s lives healthier, safer and more fulfilling. As a global medical technology company, we partner with healthcare professionals to provide best-in-class solutions and services for early detection, diagnosis and minimally invasive treatment, aiming to improve patient outcomes by elevating the standard of care in targeted disease states.

new_roles.title: Director, AI Quality, Evaluation & Observability Engineering
new_roles.description:
### **Why Patients Need You**

Pfizer's Commercial organization is putting GenAI and AI agents into work that shapes how medicines reach patients, from content creation and review to field and customer engagement. If we can't show that these systems are accurate, safe and behaving as intended, they don't belong in production. You will build the engineering capability that lets Pfizer prove it, before release and every day after.

### **What You Will Achieve**

You will own the evaluation and observability capability for AI solutions across the Commercial portfolio, and you will be accountable for the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards: the metrics, thresholds and technical criteria that inform production-readiness and ongoing monitoring decisions. You will build shared tooling, datasets and metrics that let product teams measure quality, safety and performance consistently, catch regressions before release, and detect drift and failures in production. You will set your team's priorities and decide where its engineering capacity goes across the portfolio. Success means teams evaluate through your platform by default, release decisions rest on evidence, and production AI issues are caught by monitoring before users or auditors find them.

### **How You Will Achieve It**

* Build and run a shared evaluation platform for GenAI and agentic solutions. It covers offline test suites, regression testing in CI/CD, LLM-as-judge and rubric-based scoring, and structured human review workflows.
* Set the Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, including metrics for accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, safety, bias, robustness and task success and the minimum monitoring every production AI solution must have. Calibrate automated scoring against expert human judgment and publish the agreement rates.
* Partner with commercial technology leaders to create and govern golden datasets and test sets with domain experts (e.g., medical, legal and regulatory reviewers), including versioning, data lineage and handling of sensitive data.
* Implement production observability for AI systems, including tracing of prompts, retrievals, tool calls and agent steps, plus monitoring of quality, drift, latency, cost and guardrail activity, with alerting and incident response.
* Evaluate technical and model quality, with business outcomes and value measured separately.
* Set the evaluation thresholds and technical production-readiness criteria that feed release gates run by SDLC Standards & Governance, and give a clear pass, conditional or fail assessment against them, so go-live decisions rely on measured results rather than demos.
* Partner with Responsible AI, Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity and Compliance to turn policy requirements into measurable tests and auditable evidence, including support for AI-related audits and regulatory inquiries.
* Run adversarial and red-team testing (e.g., prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage) with Cybersecurity, and feed the findings back into evaluation suites.
* Evaluate models and vendors objectively when teams select or upgrade foundation models, AI platforms or third-party AI products in partnership with Strategic Partnerships and contracting, so vendor decisions stay joined up.
* Report quality and reliability trends across the AI portfolio to senior Digital and Commercial leadership.
* Set priorities for the AI quality and observability team and allocate its engineering capacity against portfolio needs, based on risk, release timing and business impact. Make the trade-offs visible and escalate when demand exceeds capacity.
* Lead and develop a team of AI quality and observability engineers that will evolve over time, and coach product and vendor teams, including third-party and offshore partners, to own their evaluations using shared tooling.

### **Decision Rights & Escalation**

* **Decides:** Commercial AI evaluation and observability standards, metrics, thresholds and minimum monitoring requirements; the technical readiness assessment for each release; team priorities and capacity allocation; evaluation tooling and platform design within enterprise architecture standards.
* **Informs:** Release go/no-go decisions made through SDLC stage gates and product ownership; model, platform and vendor selection decisions led with Strategic Partnerships and contracting.
* **Escalates to the Commercial AI Portfolio Lead when:** a team wants to release a solution that does not meet agreed thresholds (risk acceptance); a production issue creates patient-safety, compliance or reputational exposure; demand for evaluation support exceeds team capacity across priority programs; or Responsible AI, Legal or Cybersecurity cannot agree on how a requirement becomes a test.

### **Qualifications**

**Must-Have**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience in software, ML or data engineering, including 3+ years building evaluation, testing or monitoring for ML or GenAI systems in production.
* Hands-on experience designing LLM evaluations, including rubric and LLM-as-judge methods, human evaluation design, and statistically sound comparison of model or prompt versions.
* Experience instrumenting production systems for observability (tracing, metrics, logging, alerting) and running incident response.
* Strong Python skills and experience integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
* Experience leading engineering teams and influencing product teams across a matrix without direct authority.
* Ability to explain evaluation results and their limits plainly to non-technical leaders.

**Nice-to-Have**

* Master's degree or PhD in a quantitative field.
* Experience with LLM evaluation and observability tooling (e.g., OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Arize, Weights & Biases, MLflow, Ragas, Promptfoo).
* Experience evaluating RAG systems and multi-step AI agents, including tool use and MCP-based integrations.
* Familiarity with AI risk and regulatory frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001).
* Experience with AI red-teaming or adversarial testing.
* Pharmaceutical or life sciences experience, ideally with Commercial, promotional review, medical or other regulated content.

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

**Other Job Details:**

* Last Date to Apply for Job: **December 7, 2026.**
* Ability to travel based on business needs
* This position is hybrid and requires working onsite 2 to 3 days per week

 
The annual base salary for this position ranges from $189,200.00 to $315,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 22.5% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. 
This role is posted in multiple locations. If you are applying for the role in an secondary job posting location where pay transparency regulations apply, your Talent Advisor will share the local pay information with you during the first interview.

Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility.

**Sunshine Act**

Pfizer reports payments and other transfers of value to health care providers as required by federal and state transparency laws and implementing regulations. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. If you have questions regarding this matter, please do not hesitate to contact your Talent Acquisition representative.

**EEO & Employment Eligibility**

Pfizer is committed to equal opportunity in the terms and conditions of employment for all employees and job applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity or gender expression, national origin, disability or veteran status. Pfizer also complies with all applicable national, state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements of the Immigration and Nationality Act and IRCA. Pfizer is an E-Verify employer. This position requires permanent work authorization in the United States.

Pfizer endeavors to make www.pfizer.com/careers accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process and/or interviewing, please email disabilityrecruitment@pfizer.com. This is to be used solely for accommodation requests with respect to the accessibility of our website, online application process and/or interviewing. Requests for any other reason will not be returned.

To learn more about acceptable and prohibited uses of AI during the recruitment process, please review our candidate AI-use guidelines available on Pfizer Careers.

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Architecture & Quality – Connectivity Firmware
new_roles.description:
**About Marvell**

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

**Your Team, Your Impact**

Marvell's Connectivity firmware organization delivers firmware for our connectivity and optics product lines. This role owns the full Architecture & Quality function for that portfolio. Architecture and quality operate as one integrated group, a shared resource to every firmware team and not a gate in front of them. 
 
You will set the technical architecture direction for the portfolio and hold the quality bar across it, treating the two as a single end-to-end responsibility. Architecture shapes what can be verified, and quality is how we prove it, from requirements through release and into the field. You will be accountable for how architecture decisions are made, how firmware is verified and released, and how well the firmware, hardware and systems teams work together. You will lead a global team of senior technical leaders and are expected to build depth in a function that is currently concentrated in a few people.

**What You Can Expect**

This is one function, not two. Architecture decisions set what can be tested, and quality findings feed straight back into architecture. You will own the full lifecycle from requirements and design through verification, release and field support.

**Architecture that is built to be verified**

* Product and systems architecture across the Connectivity firmware portfolio: reference architectures, standards, design reviews and technical decision records, each with testability and observability designed in.
* Product hardware interlink: the architectural contract between hardware and firmware, covering requirements, interface definition, bring-up readiness and silicon-to-firmware feedback loops, with validation criteria agreed up front.
* CMIS and optics architecture: firmware architecture for CMIS-based modules and optics products, including spec compliance, feature roadmap and interoperability, tied directly to conformance and interop test plans.
* Architecture governance that scales: lightweight review processes, clear ownership and reusable components, so teams move faster instead of waiting on reviews.

**Quality as an end-to-end discipline**

* Quality strategy that starts at requirements and architecture review, not at test execution: shift-left practices, requirements quality and design-for-test standards owned jointly with the architects.
* Software Quality Assurance (SQA) strategy and execution: test strategy, automation, regression coverage, release qualification and defect trends.
* Release readiness and quality gates for all firmware releases, with clear exit criteria and a straight, data-backed go/no-go recommendation.
* Quality metrics and reporting to Engineering leadership, Product Management and customer-facing teams.

**Closing the loop**

* Customer-escape and defect analysis that traces root causes back to architecture, interfaces and process, and turns the learning into updated patterns, standards and test coverage.
* A single set of metrics and quality signals shared across architecture, interlink, optics and SQA, so design risk and test findings are managed in one view.

**Organization**

* Lead and develop a global organization (30+).
* Grow and retain senior technical talent, and manage the pipeline, hiring, succession and career paths for architects and quality engineers.
* Build a collaborative partnership with Firmware, Hardware, Systems, Product and Program Management, and with the Optics and telemetry teams.
* Own the function's budget, headcount plan, requisitions and tooling or lab investments.

**Your Team**

You will lead a small team of senior leaders and architects who together cover the function end to end, with architecture and quality responsibilities intentionally overlapping:

* Software quality assurance and release qualification.
* Hardware and firmware interlink.
* Optics and module architecture.
* Product and systems architecture.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set a multi-year architecture and quality roadmap aligned with product and customer priorities, and drive it across engineering teams that do not report to you.
* Make and communicate hard trade-offs between schedule, scope and quality, and own the release recommendation.
* Raise the architecture bar: consistent patterns, reuse across product lines, and early detection of design risk before it becomes schedule risk.
* Shift quality left: embed test, automation and requirements quality earlier in the lifecycle, and invest in CI/CD, simulation, emulation and lab infrastructure.
* Represent Architecture & Quality in executive reviews and in technical engagements with key customers and standards bodies.
* Keep the function independent and credible: escalate quality risks directly and transparently, including when the news is unwelcome.
* Build the next layer of leadership so the function does not depend on any one person, and set clear delegation across the architecture and SQA leads.
* Manage a distributed team across time zones with clear rituals, ownership and handoffs.

**What We're Looking For**

* BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
* 15+ years in embedded firmware or systems software for semiconductor, networking or optical products, including 8+ years leading managers or senior technical leaders.
* Track record owning both architecture and quality outcomes for shipping firmware products at scale.
* Deep working knowledge of firmware architecture for connectivity or optics products, with direct experience in HW/FW co-design and silicon bring-up.
* Hands-on experience with test strategy and automation, release qualification and quality metrics for complex, customer-deployed products.
* Experience leading globally distributed teams across multiple sites and cultures, including offshore QA/SQA organizations.
* Proven executive communication: able to present risk, trade-offs and recommendations to VP-level and customer audiences.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience with CMIS and optical module firmware (for example 400G/800G and coherent or pluggable optics), and related industry standards and interoperability programs.
* Familiarity with Ethernet PHY, retimer, DSP or SerDes firmware, and with security features such as MACsec.
* Experience with secure firmware update, recovery and lifecycle practices.
* Background building or transforming an SQA organization, including automation and CI/CD maturity.
* Experience in a matrixed, platform-style organization where architecture is a shared service.

**Expected Base Pay Range (USD)**

218,850 - 327,800, $ per annum

The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.

**Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements**

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights include an employee stock purchase plan with a 2-year look back, family support programs to help balance work and home life, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and a recognition and service awards to celebrate contributions and milestones. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

**Interview Integrity**

To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

**This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.**

new_roles.title: Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality
new_roles.description:
Cambridge, MA

Development – Quality Assurance /

Full-Time /

Hybrid

 

*Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need.*

*As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at* ***ScholarRock.com*** *and follow @ScholarRock on X and on LinkedIn.*

 

**Summary of Position:**

Scholar Rock is seeking an experienced, hands-on Director, Quality Systems & Digital Quality. Reporting to the Sr Director, Global Quality Systems & Compliance, this leader is an integral part of Scholar Rock’s Quality Management System (QMS) and the GxP computerized systems and data that support it, across our commercial and early-phase pipeline. Because Scholar Rock outsources all GMP manufacturing, testing, and distribution to qualified contract organizations, this role will build and sustain a lean, risk-based, phase-appropriate QMS that meets US (FDA), EU (EMA/EU GMP), and Japan (MHLW/PMDA) requirements, ensuring that Scholar Rock’s own systems are inspection-ready and that the GxP data generated on our behalf by contract partners is reliable, complete, and traceable.

### **Position Responsibilities**

***Quality Management System***

* Partner with Quality process owners to ensure GxP digital systems effectively support QMS processes, enabling efficient, compliant, and scalable operations aligned with Scholar Rock’s evolving business needs.
* Track a focused set of key QMS performance indicators and present them in periodic quality management reviews.

 

***Digital Systems & Computer Software Assurance***

* Provide Quality oversight of Scholar Rock’s GxP computerized systems (largely cloud/SaaS, e.g., eQMS, document and training management, ERP and other GxP-relevant platforms), ensuring compliance with 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, and Japan’s ER/ES guideline.
* Lead and execute GxP system enhancements and continuous improvement initiatives, partnering with business process owners to define requirements, evaluate solutions, manage implementation, and ensure effective adoption of new functionality.
* Establish and apply a risk-based computerized system validation and assurance approach consistent with applicable GxP regulatory requirements, leveraging GAMP 5 principles, relevant FDA guidance, and vendor documentation to ensure appropriate assurance while minimizing redundant testing.
* Oversee the GxP computerized system lifecycle, including risk-based validation and assurance, change control, periodic reviews, access management, audit trail controls, data retention, and system retirement. Ensure appropriate validation deliverables, testing, and documented evidence are established and maintained throughout the system lifecycle.
* Partner with IT and business owners on system selection, implementation, upgrades, and vendor releases so that new digital capabilities are adopted with right-sized assurance.
* Support qualification of computerized system suppliers (e.g., SaaS, software, and IT service providers), including risk-based vendor assessments and audits, and the Part 11/Annex 11 and data integrity provisions of their quality agreements; qualification of GMP manufacturing and testing suppliers remains with other Quality functions.
* Monitor evolving expectations, including the revision of EU GMP Annex 11 and emerging guidance on AI in GxP settings, and advise on practical, compliant adoption of digital and AI-enabled tools.
* Support the implementation of AI-enabled tools in GxP processes (e.g., document drafting and review, deviation and complaint trending, AI features within eQMS and other platforms), defining risk-based assurance, human oversight, and data integrity controls proportionate to each tool’s intended use and impact on product quality and patient safety.
* Partner with IT, Legal, and business owners to establish lightweight governance for AI use in GxP activities, including an inventory of AI applications, acceptable-use expectations, training, and ongoing performance monitoring.
* Lead the development and execution of a risk-based digital Quality roadmap, prioritizing system enhancements and improvements based on business needs, compliance requirements, and operational efficiencies.
* Partner with Quality process owners and cross-functional stakeholders to identify improvement opportunities, translate business needs into functional requirements, and implement scalable digital solutions.
* Drive the end-to-end implementation of GxP system enhancements, including requirements definition, risk assessments, configuration, testing, validation documentation, deployment, and post-implementation support.
* Establish efficient processes for managing system changes, including vendor releases, impact assessments, regression testing, and maintaining systems in a validated state.
* Provide hands-on leadership and technical guidance for Veeva eQMS, eDMS, and other GxP platforms, ensuring effective system functionality, integration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear system ownership, governance, and accountability across Quality, IT, and business functions, including responsibilities for system administration, validation, user access, and ongoing lifecycle management.
* Support regulatory inspections and audits involving computerized systems, electronic records, electronic signatures, and data integrity, including preparation of supporting documentation and remediation of identified gaps.
* Drive effective adoption of new digital capabilities through stakeholder engagement, training, change management, and ongoing evaluation of system effectiveness.
* Establish and maintain effective governance for GxP system enhancements and vendor releases, including change prioritization, impact assessments, testing strategies, implementation planning, and post-deployment monitoring.

 

***Data Integrity & Data Governance***

* Lead the development and ongoing governance of Scholar Rock’s GxP data integrity program, establishing risk-based expectations, controls, and oversight mechanisms in partnership with business process owners and applicable Quality functions.
* Define a lightweight data governance model with clear data ownership and stewardship for GxP data across Quality, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical.
* Extend data integrity oversight to contract organizations through quality agreement requirements, data integrity–focused audit criteria, and review of partner-generated data (e.g., batch records, CoAs, stability, deviations).
* Establish governance and controls for GxP-relevant master data, partnering with designated data owners to ensure data accuracy, consistency, integrity, and appropriate alignment across internal systems, contract partners, and regulatory information.
* Lead data integrity risk assessments and drive timely, proportionate remediation of gaps.

 

***Inspection Readiness & Regulatory Support***

* Lead inspection readiness for the QMS, computerized systems, and data integrity controls, and support health authority inspections of Scholar Rock and its contract partners.
* Contribute to regulatory submissions and responses, such as annual reports, IND/CTA updates, and marketing applications in the US, EU, and Japan.
* Maintain awareness of regulatory changes in the US, EU, and Japan and translate them into practical, minimal-necessary updates to the QMS.

 

***Leadership & Partnership***

* Act as the subject matter expert and coach for colleagues across Quality and partner functions on QMS, computerized system, and data integrity topics.
* Collaborate with the Head of Global Quality and Quality leadership, IT, Regulatory, Technical Operations, and Clinical to align quality systems with corporate goals and regulatory obligations.
* Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and data integrity, and serve as a change agent for simplification and digitization of the QMS.

### **Candidate Requirements**

* BS/MS degree in a scientific, engineering, or information systems discipline.
* 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry, with 5+ years leading Quality systems, computerized system compliance, or related programs; biologics experience preferred.
* Deep understanding of GxP and Quality System requirements (US, EU, and Japan) for biologics development and commercial products, including ICH Q9(R1) and Q10.
* Demonstrated expertise in 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, risk-based CSA/GAMP 5, and global data integrity expectations, including qualification of computerized system and SaaS suppliers.
* Familiarity with AI/ML-enabled tools in regulated environments and with emerging health authority expectations for AI use in GxP activities.
* Experience in a virtual or outsourced model, including oversight of quality systems and data integrity at CDMOs and contract testing laboratories.
* Experience leading or supporting regulatory inspections and interfacing with global health authorities.
* Proven ability to design lean, simple processes and to make pragmatic, risk-based decisions on what is required versus nice to have.
* Highly proactive, decisive, and capable of independently managing key initiatives as a hands-on individual contributor.
* Collaborative leader who builds quality culture and capability across teams through influence, coaching, and knowledge sharing.
* Excellent communication skills and ability to influence across functions and with external partners.

$200,000 - $260,000 a year

*Scholar Rock is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees*.

new_roles.title: Director, Quality Assurance Operations
new_roles.description:
**Director, Quality Assurance Operations**

At Vericel Corporation, we are pioneers in advanced cell therapies for sports medicine and severe burn care, transforming patient lives through cutting-edge regenerative medicine. Our commitment to innovation, patient-centered focus, and scientific excellence drives us to develop groundbreaking treatments including MACI (knee cartilage repair), Epicel and Nexobrid (burn care).

**Position Summary**

The Director of Quality Operations is responsible for the strategic leadership and performance of Quality Assurance Operations, Document Control, and Supplier Quality Management. This role provides oversight of product disposition and release, labeling and documentation controls, deviations, CAPAs, product complaints, supplier quality management, tech transfer activities, controlled documentation, and internal audits. The Director translates business objectives and quality risks into operational strategies, resource plans, and measurable outcomes. This position develops organizational capability through effective leadership, succession planning, and talent development while driving cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement. The Director exercises independent, risk-based decision-making within delegated authority to ensure compliance, operational excellence, and sustained product quality.

**Schedule:** This position is onsite Monday through Friday at our Burlington office, with one day per week at our Cambridge office.

**Essential Functions:**

**Quality Operations and Department Management**

* Provide strategic oversight and accountability for product disposition and release, deviations, CAPAs, complaints, supplier quality management, documentation controls, labeling review, and internal audit programs and tech transfer activities; ensure activities are executed in compliance with regulatory requirements and business objectives.
* Establish department strategy and annual operating plans aligned with organizational priorities, quality objectives, and risk management principles; determine resource, staffing, and budget requirements to support business growth and compliance commitments.
* Serve as the Quality Operations representative in cross-functional governance, planning, and decision-making forums involving Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Technical Operations, Product Development, and Project Management.
* Make and oversee complex quality decisions within delegated authority using scientific rationale, regulatory requirements, and risk-based assessments; escalate significant compliance or product quality risks with recommended mitigation strategies.
* Develop, implement, and maintain departmental policies, procedures, standards, and governance processes to ensure consistent and effective execution across all areas of responsibility.
* Ensure continuous inspection readiness; lead departmental support for regulatory inspections, customer audits, and internal audits, and ensure timely completion of all commitments and corrective actions.

**Continuous Improvement and Quality Metrics**

new_roles.description:
Division Department: Therapeutics | Quality

Position Title: Director of Quality (Head of Quality)

Reports To: Corporate Head of Quality (proposed; final reporting structure to be confirmed)

Salary - $225-250,000 based on experience

**PharmaLogic is expanding our therapeutics business line. Our therapeutics business, Agilera, is the** **world’s only cGMP-compliant CDMO currently manufacturing and distributing commercial radiopharmaceutical therapeutics across more than 30 countries. In this role,** **you will have the opportunity to work as part of a unique environment that is involved in the entire value chain, from the preclinical phase to the commercial production and distribution of radiopharmaceuticals.**

**Role Summary:**

The Director of Quality serves as the Head of Quality for PharmaLogic’s newly acquired therapeutics business, leading the quality organization and establishing the systems, capabilities, and culture needed for reliable GMP manufacturing. This leader is accountable for the pharmaceutical quality system and Quality oversight of sterile therapeutic drug manufacturing, testing, and release under applicable 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 requirements. As a member of the site leadership team, the Director partners with Operations, Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, and corporate Quality to support clinical supply, technology transfer, commercialization, and growth. The role requires independent judgment, visible leadership on the manufacturing floor, and the ability to translate quality requirements into practical execution while protecting patient safety and product quality.

**Job Responsibilities and Duties:**

**Quality Leadership and Governance**

Lead the Quality function, including Quality Assurance and oversight of Quality Control and microbiology activities within the assigned organizational scope. Set strategy, staffing, budgets, objectives, and development plans; build a capable team with clear accountability.

Maintain the Quality unit’s independent authority to approve or reject materials and drug products, including outsourced products; approve quality-impacting procedures and specifications; and ensure documented responsibilities and appropriate escalation to corporate Quality and executive leadership.

Own batch disposition through authorized Quality personnel. Ensure production and laboratory records, deviations, and required test results receive appropriate review before release. Place materials or product on hold and stop affected operations when quality or compliance concerns warrant.

**Quality Systems and Sterile Manufacturing**

Establish and continuously improve systems for deviations, investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, document control, training, complaints, product quality reviews, and quality risk management. Require scientifically sound root-cause analysis and verification of CAPA effectiveness.

Provide Quality oversight of aseptic processing and contamination control, including cleanrooms, environmental and personnel monitoring, gowning qualification, aseptic process simulations, sterilization, disinfection, and container closure integrity, as applicable.

Oversee laboratory controls, specifications, analytical method validation and transfer, stability programs, and investigations of out-of-specification and out-of-trend results. Ensure complete, accurate, traceable data and effective controls for electronic records and computerized systems.

Approve qualification and validation strategies, protocols, and reports for facilities, utilities, equipment, manufacturing processes, cleaning, and computerized systems. Ensure a documented lifecycle approach and continued process verification.

**Manufacturing Readiness and External Partners**

Lead Quality readiness for new products, technology transfers, process scale-up, and commercial launches. Establish clear acceptance criteria and readiness decisions with Development, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.

Serve as the primary site Quality representative for FDA inspections and customer audits. Lead inspection preparation, responses, and commitments; maintain sustained readiness and timely, effective remediation.

Manage supplier qualification, contract laboratory and manufacturer oversight, audits, and quality agreements. Define responsibilities with CDMO customers and ensure outsourced activities meet agreed quality requirements.

**Acquisition Integration and Regulatory Partnership**

Lead the acquisition Quality integration plan: assess inherited systems and commitments, prioritize gaps by risk, align governance and procedures with corporate standards, and manage changes without disrupting compliant product supply.

Partner with Regulatory Affairs on manufacturing and quality content for filings, change assessments, and regulatory commitments. Lead quality defect assessments and support recalls, field actions, and required notifications with designated functions.

For radiopharmaceutical therapeutics, oversee appropriate controls for isotope and precursor quality, radiochemical testing, time-sensitive manufacturing and disposition, and stability. Partner with Radiation Safety and EHS on safe, compliant execution.

**Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement**

Present quality performance and material risks to site and corporate leadership. Use management reviews and meaningful metrics to improve investigation quality, CAPA effectiveness, release reliability, training, and inspection readiness.

**Job Requirements, Skills and Education:**

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, microbiology, pharmacy, engineering, or a related scientific discipline.

Typically, 10 or more years of progressive pharmaceutical Quality experience, including at least 5 years leading teams or major Quality programs in a GMP manufacturing environment.

Demonstrated Quality leadership in sterile injectable manufacturing, with substantial knowledge of aseptic processing, contamination control, laboratory controls, validation, and data integrity.

**Strong working knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, applicable electronic records requirements, and relevant FDA guidance and ICH quality principles.**

Experience leading regulatory inspections, complex investigations, remediation, and batch disposition, with sound scientific judgment and the ability to defend quality decisions.

Experience supporting technology transfer, clinical or commercial manufacturing, and cross-functional delivery of significant quality or operational improvements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Experience with therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals or radioligand therapies; CDMO operations and pharmaceutical customer partnerships; and commercial launch or preapproval inspection readiness.

Experience integrating an acquisition, building or transforming a quality organization, and implementing electronic quality management systems. Advanced scientific degree or relevant professional certification.

**Leadership and Working Expectations**

A visible, hands-on leader who develops people, communicates clearly, and holds teams accountable. Able to challenge decisions constructively, escalate risks promptly, and make timely decisions under pressure. Regular onsite presence in manufacturing and laboratory areas, compliance with required gowning and safety practices, and availability for critical quality events are expected. Travel requirements will be defined for the role. Essential functions may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

Come join our winning team and begin a fulfilling career with us by applying today. 
 
PharmaLogic is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other protected class.

**Benefits Include:**

401(k) retirement benefit program

Medical

Dental care

Disability insurance

Employee assistance program

Life insurance

On-site parking

Paid time off

Vision care

**Your Job:**

 

The Director of Quality is responsible for the overall operations of quality management throughout the Medical Center. Ensures that the hospital's policies and practices as related to patient care are within appropriate guidelines as designated by all State and Federal agencies as well as certifying agencies. Facilitates the hospital's JCAHO compliance and survey readiness. Acts as a resource to members of the management team in reference to legal guidelines for Patient Care Services.

 
 

**Your Job Requirements:**

new_roles.description:
Overview:

**Hospital Name: Ohiohealth Rehabilitation Hospital** 
**Joint venture/Partnership/Affiliation with Select Medical** 
**Position:** **Director of Quality Management** 
**Location: Dublin, OH**

* Bonus incentives
* Extensive onboarding and training program
* Customizable health insurance packages

**Who We Are**

Our inpatient rehabilitation hospital is committed to providing exceptional and compassionate care to best address the medical, physical, emotional, and vocational challenges for individuals with brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, neurological disorders, orthopedic issues, amputation, and multiple traumas

Responsibilities:

Coordinates the Medical Quality Management and Performance Improvement activities to measurably enhance the quality, process and cost effectiveness of patient and customer services rendered. Coordinates the Performance Improvement and Patient Safety programs in accordance with the guidelines and regulatory requirements of Federal and State regulations on a hospital-wide basis. Oversees operations of the Infection Control and Employee Health Programs. Develops and Reviews policies and procedures to ensure compliance with all regulatory and accrediting standards. Collects data to monitor compliance and/or trends.

 

* Institutes and monitors the Hospital’s CQI Processes, utilizing data analysis measuring tools. Oversight/coordination of operations of the Infection Control & Employee Health Program based upon hospital size and configuration.
* Assists with the design and compliance of quality processes/activities in the areas of clinical/medical staff PI for all applicable clinical/medical TJC /CARF/DOH standards. Assists with all assigned activities to assure that the hospital maintains accreditation, certification and licensure. Assumes leadership with the Joint Commission and DOH as well as other regulatory agencies with regard to CQI activities.
* Serves as a resource for all departments within the facility to provide guidance on designing, implementing, analyzing and reporting on Quality Improvement.
* Assists clinical areas in developing criteria, monitoring and reporting mechanisms and action documentation related to the hospital’s CQI program.
* Performs basic chart review activities with appropriate staff for outcome utilization, infection control and medical CQI indicators. Analyzes results of chart review activities with appropriate staff and confers with department staff on any case requiring special attention.
* Prepares analysis of significant PI findings pertaining to adverse drug reactions, drug usage evaluation, medical management of acute transfers and other CQI indicators.

Qualifications:

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Registered Nurse with valid state license. Legacy employees may exist with other clinical licensure.
* Requires experience in at least one of the core areas of responsibility: Quality, Survey Readiness, Risk Management, Infection Control, Employee Health and Education
* Demonstrates familiarity with accrediting standards, including TJC and CARF preferred.

**Preferred Experience**

* Previous experience in Quality Improvement, with Statistical Process Control experience and computer skills preferred.
* Demonstrates familiarity with accrediting standards, including JCAHO and CARF preferred.
* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) preferred

Additional Data:

* Start Strong: Extensive and thorough orientation program to ensure a smooth transition into our setting
* Recharge & Refresh: Generous PTO and Paid Sick Time for full-time team members to maintain a healthy work-life balance
* Your Health Matters: Comprehensive medical/RX, health, vision, employee assistance program (EAP) and dental plan offerings for full-time team members
* Invest in Your Future: Company-matching 401(k) retirement plan, as well as life and disability protection for full-time team members
* Your Impact Matters: Join a team of over 44,000 committed to providing exceptional patient care

*Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disabled/Veterans*
