new_roles.title: Director, Loyalty Strategy & Operations
new_roles.description:
At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business.

 

Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere.

**Introduction to the role**
----------------------------

 

The Director of Loyalty Strategy & Operations will own Brand Expedia's loyalty strategy and operational delivery globally, while also leading the cross-brand element of loyalty across Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo.

 

Reporting directly to the VP of Customer Growth & Loyalty for Brand Expedia, this role is best suited to a strategic thinker with a deep understanding of loyalty program best practices, program economics, and operational scaling.

 

You will bring a data-driven approach and an analytical mindset to dive into insights, listen to travelers, and uncover growth opportunities that ladder up to our broader organizational goals.

 

Close collaboration with Brand Expedia leadership and cross-brand partners is essential to align loyalty strategy with brand-specific goals and key performance indicators. This role regularly interfaces with executive (SVP+ and C-level) leadership as well as cross-functional partners across all levels, requiring authentic relationship-building and strong stakeholder alignment.

 

Additionally, this role proactively identifies opportunities to improve traveler journeys, elevate engagement, and strengthen brand loyalty through continuous enhancements to current offerings, prioritizing simplicity, operational rigor, and traveler comprehension.

 

Finally, this role is external-facing and engages with key strategic partners and third-party entities, fostering high-impact relationships to elevate the Brand Expedia traveler experience.

 

**In this role, you will:**

 

**Strategic Vision & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Own the vision and develop strategies to grow and strengthen customer relationships, repeat bookings, and long-term stickiness through Brand Expedia loyalty and customer growth initiatives.
* Drive a comprehensive loyalty and customer growth agenda, aligning program value propositions with short-term incentives, lifecycle touchpoints, and personalized member experiences.
* Manage and strengthen cross-functional relationships across Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo to ensure tight alignment between loyalty operations and brand strategy.
* Act as an energetic advocate for loyalty at every level, connecting program strategy back to the company's broader business objectives and ensuring loyalty has a clear voice across the organization.
* Flex effortlessly between high-level strategic vision and detailed operational execution, knowing when to dive into mechanics and when to empower your team.
* Utilize market research, customer insights, competitor intelligence, and behavioral data analytics to identify high-potential customer segments and personalize member engagement.
* Design, implement, and optimize loyalty offerings and operational workflows to ensure they deliver tangible customer value and achieve business targets.
* Serve as the dedicated voice of the traveler, partnering closely with brand marketing, product development, and member experience teams.
* Balance agile, short-term experimentation (such as rapid test-and-learn initiatives) with scalable, long-term programmatic frameworks.
* Collaborate closely with Loyalty Performance, Finance, and Analytics teams on program economics, business casing, and measurement, while partnering with Product, Technology, and Experience Design (XD) to deliver seamless end-to-end traveler journeys.
Coordinate with CRM, Integrated Marketing, Research & Insights, and commercial teams to drive cohesive execution across channels. 

 

**Team Leadership & Operational Stewardship**

* Lead, inspire, and grow a high-performing organization of 6 team members, including direct management of 3 Senior Managers, cultivating an inclusive, innovative environment with a "Go Get What's Next" mindset.
* Guide team operations, resource allocation, and project roadmaps to ensure seamless delivery across all strategic loyalty streams.
* Empower team members to move quickly, resolve roadblocks independently, and drive measurable outcomes with clarity.
* Unlock each team member's full potential, supporting individualized development paths and career progression.
* Build trust, positive momentum, and mutual accountability across the team and with executive stakeholders.
Balance workloads effectively so all team members are fully engaged and given meaningful opportunities to stretch their leadership capabilities. 

 

**Experience & Qualifications:**

* 10+ years of relevant experience in loyalty strategy, customer lifecycle marketing, or commercial growth, with a bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
* 5+ years of demonstrated people leadership experience, with proven success managing people leaders (e.g. Senior Managers) and developing high-performing teams.
* Proven track record leading large-scale, global loyalty programs and complex operational workstreams that deliver exceptional business outcomes.
* Deep domain expertise in modern loyalty strategies, customer retention, motivational mechanics, and incentive design.
* Strong business acumen and analytical capability to interpret complex data, model program economics, and make decisive, value-generating decisions.
* Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships across diverse groups, including Product, Technology, Analytics, Finance, Supply, Brand Marketing, and Customer Operations.
* Exceptional communication and executive presence, with a proven ability to influence, socialize recommendations, and drive alignment at all leadership levels.
* Passion for designing delightful customer experiences and driving customer retention through customer-centric, data-grounded approaches.
* Thrives in a dynamic, collaborative environment, managing multiple priorities with sound judgment, adaptability, and high attention to detail.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and modern collaboration tools.
* Experience with Tableau or similar business intelligence and analytics platforms.
Proactive curiosity and ability to leverage modern AI tools to streamline processes, automate repetitive tasks, and elevate team efficiency. 

 
The total cash range for this position in New York is $224,000.00 to $313,500.00. Employees in this role have the potential to increase their pay up to $358,500.00, which is the top of the range, based on ongoing, demonstrated, and sustained performance in the role.
The total cash range for this position in Seattle is $207,500.00 to $290,500.00. Employees in this role have the potential to increase their pay up to $332,000.00, which is the top of the range, based on ongoing, demonstrated, and sustained performance in the role. 
 

Starting pay for this role will vary based on multiple factors, including location, available budget, and an individual’s knowledge, skills, and experience. Pay ranges may be modified in the future.

 

**Benefits and perks**

Expedia Group offers benefits and perks designed to support employees and their families, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, an Employee Assistance Program, wellness and travel reimbursement, travel discounts, and International Airlines Travel Agent Network (IATAN) membership. Learn more about life at Expedia Group at https://careers.expediagroup.com/life .

 

**Accommodation requests**

Expedia Group is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruiting experience. If you need an accommodation or adjustment due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a request at https://expedia.service-now.com/askeg?id=job\_accommodation .

 

**About Expedia Group**

new_roles.title: Director, Information Technology Procurement Management (Director, Procurement Systems and Operations)
new_roles.description:
**About NYC Health + Hospitals**
--------------------------------

 

NYC Health + Hospitals is the largest public health care system in the United States. We provide essential outpatient, inpatient and home-based services to more than one million New Yorkers every year across the city’s five boroughs. Our large health system consists of ambulatory centers, acute care centers, post-acute care/long-term care, rehabilitation programs, Home Care, and Correctional Health Services. Our diverse workforce is uniquely focused on empowering New Yorkers.

At NYC Health + Hospitals, our mission is to deliver high quality care health services, without exception. Every employee takes a person-centered approach that exemplifies the ICARE values (Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence) through empathic communication and partnerships between all persons.

**Work Shifts**
---------------

 

**9:00 A.M – 5:00 P.M**

**Duties & Responsibilities**
-----------------------------

 

SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

1. Strategic Planning

* Lead the indirect procurement function by developing and executing a comprehensive strategy to optimize spend across diverse non-clinical categories
* Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to align procurement strategies with organizational goals and operational priorities
* Utilize data analytics and market intelligence to identify opportunities for cost savings, process improvements, and supplier consolidation
* Develop operating procedures, internal policies, and training guides to support consistent procurement practices
* Partner with internal stakeholders to create scopes of work, request for proposals, and other solicitation documents

2. Operational Performance

* Oversee contracting, monitor contract compliance, and manage vendor relationships to ensure optimal pricing, service levels, and risk mitigation
* Drive cost-savings initiatives while maintaining compliance with healthcare regulations, organizational policies, and industry standards
* Manage capital procurement activities in coordination with internal and external partners throughout planning, budgeting, project management, and transactional phases
* Monitor supplier performance, manage risks, and resolve issues promptly to maintain uninterrupted service and supply
* Develop and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) related to savings, supplier performance, and process efficiency
* Prioritize procurement activities to meet end-user deadlines and expectations
* Develop and deliver executive briefings to senior leadership, providing insights on supply chain performance, risk mitigation, and strategic opportunities
* Perform related duties as required to support departmental and organizational objectives

3. Staff Development

* Train and lead a high-performing procurement team focused on operational excellence and professional growth
* Foster a collaborative and innovative team culture that encourages continuous learning and improvement
* Implement training programs to enhance team skills in strategic sourcing, contract management, and vendor relations
* Promote effective communication and engagement across all levels of the organization

4. Financial Management

* Lead spend reduction initiatives and ensure effective financial management of indirect procurement budgets
* Collaborate with finance and project teams to ensure accurate budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting
* Conduct procurement audits and risk assessments to maintain fiscal discipline and compliance
* Utilize financial data to track savings realization, cost avoidance, and return on investment

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

 

1. Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in Business Administration, Computer Science,
 
Management or other related discipline from an accredited college or university; and six (6) years of satisfactory,
 
full-time paid responsible experience in information processing, program management, systems development or
 
related activity in a large governmental agency, hospital or health care facility, or hospital-related business firm,
 
three (3) years of which must have been in a managerial capacity; or
 
2. Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in disciplines, as listed in “1” above, and five (5) years of
 
experience, as described in #2 above, one (1) year of which must have been in a managerial capacity; or
 
3. A satisfactory equivalent combination of education and experience.

**Department Preferences**
--------------------------

* Indirect and Non-Clinical Spend Categories
* Strategic Sourcing
* Contract Negotiation
* Vendor Management

**Benefits**
------------

 

NYC Health and Hospitals offers a competitive benefits package that includes:

* Comprehensive Health Benefits for employees hired to work 20+ hrs. per week
* Retirement Savings and Pension Plans
* Paid Holidays and Vacation in accordance with employees' Collectively bargained contracts
* Loan Forgiveness Programs for eligible employees
* College tuition discounts and professional development opportunities
* College Savings Program
* Union Benefits for eligible titles
* Multiple employee discounts programs
* Commuter Benefits Programs

**How To Apply**
----------------

 

If you wish to apply for this position, please apply online by clicking the "Apply for Job" button.

new_roles.title: Operations Director, Curriculum & School Support
new_roles.description:
**About K12 Coalition**

K12 Coalition provides products and services that help K-12 schools and teachers achieve transformational learning outcomes. We tackle many of today’s toughest education obstacles, including teacher certification, test preparation, professional learning, curriculum, consulting, and strategic planning. K12 Coalition came together when educators with deep experience as teachers, school leaders, and high-level district administrators observed a genuine need for something better. Our divisions include iteach, Passage Preparation, Professional Development Institute, Teaching Channel, Lavinia Group, and Keys to Literacy.

 

**About Lavinia Group**

Lavinia Group is dedicated to driving meaningful academic improvements in K-12 education through instructional coaching, professional learning, high-quality curriculum, strategic planning, and summer school support that enhances educator effectiveness and strengthens student outcomes.

 

With deep expertise in school leadership, curriculum implementation, and instructional best practices, Lavinia Group delivers tailored, research-based solutions to meet the evolving needs of our partners. Guided by a commitment to equity, instructional excellence, and long-term capacity building, we work alongside educators and district leaders through hands-on coaching, immersive training, and collaborative partnerships. Our mission is to help schools achieve transformational learning outcomes that endure beyond our direct support.

 

**Employment Type:**

* Full-Time
* Exempt
* Salaried

 

**Location:** Remote, available from anywhere within the U.S.

 

**The Opportunity**

Lavinia Group, a division of K12 Coalition, is seeking an Operations Director, Curriculum & School Support to build and lead the systems that bring our curriculum and professional learning services to schools. The largest focus of this role is managing the full operational lifecycle of our print curriculum, from demand forecasting and inventory planning to production, fulfillment, and direct customer support. This role also leads operational planning for digital curriculum, professional learning, and consultant staffing outside of our RISE summer learning program.

 

This is an opportunity to help shape how a newly structured operations team works together. Partnering with the Managing Director, Operations and fellow operations leaders, you will help establish clear responsibilities, shared processes, and scalable systems across Lavinia Group while leading execution within your own portfolio. You will turn product and service priorities into practical plans, use technology and AI to improve workflows, and build the operational foundation for new offerings and continued growth.

 

The Operations Director, Curriculum & School Support reports to the Managing Director, Operations and directly manages a Senior Associate, Operations. This role is ideal for an operations leader who enjoys building structure, solving complex delivery challenges, and staying closely involved in day-to-day execution.

 

**What You’ll Do**

Print Curriculum & Fulfillment Operations

* Lead the full print curriculum workflow, including demand forecasting, inventory planning, production schedules, ordering, and fulfillment.
* Partner with Sales and Curriculum teams to translate sales projections, partner needs, and product timelines into purchasing and production plans.
* Manage print vendors, book vendors, and fulfillment partners, including negotiations, performance monitoring, and issue resolution against quality, cost, and delivery expectations.
* Monitor inventory and fulfillment costs, anticipating shortages, excess stock, and delivery risks and adjusting plans as needs change.
* Provide direct customer support for curriculum orders and delivery questions, coordinating timely resolution of fulfillment issues and keeping partners informed.

Operational Systems & Product Implementation

* Build and improve the systems, workflows, and project plans that support curriculum and professional learning development, implementation, and delivery.
* Partner with Curriculum, Product, and Technology teams to define operational requirements for digital curriculum platforms and coordinate improvements that support users and internal teams.
* Establish consistent partner onboarding processes and coordinate operational readiness for product launches, updates, and retirements.
* Use technology, automation, and AI-enabled tools to reduce manual work, improve visibility, and create more reliable, scalable workflows.
* Partner with fellow operations leaders to establish shared practices, clarify team handoffs, and resolve dependencies across Lavinia Group.

Professional Learning & Consultant Staffing

* Lead operational planning for partner-facing professional learning and coaching services, aligning schedules, staffing, resources, and delivery requirements.
* Develop and maintain staffing and capacity plans, partnering with academic and service leaders to forecast facilitator, consultant, and content-development needs.
* Manage consultant staffing and utilization in Hub Planner, maintaining accurate assignments and availability and addressing capacity gaps with relevant leaders.
* Manage workflows for custom professional learning requests, pricing, and approvals in partnership with academic and business leaders.
* Establish operational delivery standards and monitor utilization, delivery days, and partner feedback to identify and implement improvements.

Budget & Performance Management

* Build and manage curriculum, product, and professional learning operating budgets in partnership with the Managing Director, Operations and relevant business leaders.
* Monitor spending, delivery costs, and budget performance, recommending adjustments that align resources with demand and organizational priorities.
* Maintain reporting that gives leaders clear visibility into inventory, fulfillment, staffing capacity, and operational performance.
* Coordinate with finance and sales operations colleagues to ensure accurate information and clear handoffs for invoicing, contracting, and vendor onboarding.

Team Leadership

* Manage and develop the Senior Associate, Operations, setting clear priorities, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
* Provide ongoing coaching and feedback, delegate work effectively, and support professional growth while maintaining accountability for team deliverables.

Other Duties

* Support the team with additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to help meet evolving organizational goals and objectives.

* Bachelor’s degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* At least 5 years of experience in operations, product operations, supply chain, or a related field, including managing complex, cross-functional initiatives.
* Direct experience managing operations for physical products sold to customers, including demand forecasting, inventory planning, production or purchasing coordination, and fulfillment.
* Experience managing vendors and fulfillment partners, including monitoring costs, quality, and delivery performance and resolving customer issues.
* Demonstrated success building scalable operational systems and workflows, including defining operational requirements, partnering across teams to implement improvements, and using AI-enabled tools and automation to reduce manual work.
* Experience managing budgets, analyzing operational data, and developing staffing, capacity, or resource plans.
* Experience managing and developing direct reports, including setting priorities, delegating work, and providing performance feedback.
* Advanced proficiency in Google Workspace, particularly Google Sheets, for forecasting, reporting, data analysis, and operational decision-making, along with experience using project management or workflow tools.
* Strong project management and communication skills, with the ability to coordinate across teams, manage competing priorities, and follow through on commitments.
* Experience in K–12 education, curriculum publishing, or professional learning is preferred but not required.

**How We Work at K12 Coalition**

Our work is grounded in five Core Competencies that guide how we collaborate, support others, and move work forward: Accountability, Adaptability, Collaboration, Customer Service Orientation, and Initiative.

* **Accountability:** Following through on work, owning commitments, and communicating progress or challenges along the way.
* **Adaptability:** Navigating change with flexibility and focus as priorities, information, or needs shift.
* **Collaboration:** Working together across roles and perspectives to achieve shared goals.
* **Customer Service Orientation:** Meeting the needs of internal and external partners with clarity, responsiveness, and follow-through.
* **Initiative:** Taking action without waiting to be asked and looking for ways to improve systems, processes, or experiences.

 

**Compensation Philosophy**

As part of our commitment to maintaining fair and consistent compensation practices, new hires are typically brought into the organization at a salary between the band minimum and midpoint, based on their qualifications, location, internal alignment, and the budgeted amount for the role.

 

**Why Work with Us**

We believe in supporting the whole employee by offering a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet diverse needs. Our full-time employee benefits include flexible time off, paid parental leave, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, and a 401(k) with company matching. We are committed to fostering a work environment that promotes both personal and professional well-being.

 

**Our Typical Selection Process**

Our selection process typically includes an online application, a short phone interview, a hiring manager interview, a candidate exercise, and a final interview.

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

K12 Coalition is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you need assistance or accommodation during the interview process due to a disability, please email us at recruitingteam@k12coalition.com. This information will be treated as confidential and used only for the purpose of determining an appropriate accommodation for the interview process.

 

**Protecting Your Job Search**

K12 Coalition is committed to a transparent and secure recruitment process. Please keep the following in mind as you explore opportunities with us:

* **Official communication:** All recruitment-related communication will come from an @k12coalition.com email address. We do not use messaging platforms for recruiting.
* **Application process:** We do not send unsolicited job offers. All open positions are listed on our official Careers Page, and any offer follows a formal interview process.
* **No upfront payments:** We will never ask candidates to pay fees of any kind during the hiring process, including for training materials, background checks, or equipment.

 

If you receive any communication that does not align with the above, please report it to recruitingteam@k12coalition.com.

new_roles.title: Director, Warehouse Operations
new_roles.description:
Role Overview:

The Director, Warehouse Operations is accountable for effectively managing US warehousing operations to include receiving, shipping, transfers, inventory control, labor management, and safeguarding Brother assets. The position is accountable for the Warehouse Operations budget to control costs and to reduce expenditures without compromising the operation’s capabilities to service customers. The Director, Warehouse Operations is accountable for the development and implementation of continuous improvement initiatives that will enable operational efficiencies across all warehouses to improve customer satisfaction and savings. This position creates an environment of collaboration and respect among the various departments such as Finance, Information Technology (IT) and Transportation to drive overall supply chain excellence throughout the delivery process.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Operations Management

* + Oversee daily warehouse operations within the Brother distribution network (East Coast, West Coast, Tennessee, etc.)
 + Drive improvement through collaboration and analysis; support manufacturing, channel partners, and end-users
 + Monitor all warehousing operations in designated external warehouses while utilizing best practices
 + Ensure shipment compliance including the quality, timing and accurate delivery of products
 + Drive performance results through the management of the third partly logistics provider
 + Provide direction, leadership and guidance to leadership staff and monitor the efficiency, knowledge and skill sets of the staff and provide the necessary guidance, training, coaching, feedback and appraisal as necessary
 + Create an environment of collaboration, innovation, problem-solving and continuous improvement
 + Foster inventory strategies that deliver improvements in productivity, quality, and cost
 + Identify the best way to ensure correct inventory management by creating a robust repeatable process including the latest technology
 + Develop, direct, and manage overall improvement targets and oversee execution of initiatives
 + Work closely with the Supply Chain Planning team to guarantee “hot items” are available at the Warehouse to satisfy customer demand
 + Work closely with the Inbound / Outbound Transportation teams to guarantee “hot containers” and/or “hot orders” are managed by aligned Customer Service Levels Agreements

Strategic Direction

* + Develop an overall plan from the current state to the future state that meets business and customer requirements for best-in-class service for inventory, warehousing operations and delivery
 + Assess current and future operational risks locally, and translate those into strategies, capabilities, best practices, and key performance indicators (KPIs)
 + Develop and deploy inventory and operations performance standards that support and align with company strategy and customer expectations across the distribution network
 + Develop a continuous improvement approach across the warehouse operations organization to challenge the operational “status quo” and optimize operational cost and service
 + Partner with the HR, IT, Procurement and Financial teams to address open issues and develop best-in-class cross functional practices, processes, metrics, and reports for the warehouse operations area
 + Work closely with the Supply Chain Planning team to plan for future warehouse space for efficient utilization to minimize expenses
 + Work closely with the Inbound / Outbound Transportation teams to develop joint plans to improve customer service levels and operational costs
 + Work closely with the order management team to define “Total Order Cycle” optimization initiatives to improve customer satisfaction and operational costs

Provider and Vendor Management

* + Conduct monthly and quarterly business reviews (MBR & QBR) with all 3rd party providers to ensure consistent Service Levels are met and business and customer needs are addressed
 + Partner with the procurement organization to manage vendor relationships and pricing agreements for warehousing services
 + Ensure business and customer service commitments are being upheld and address deficiencies accordingly
 + Develop a continuous improvement approach with all 3rd party providers to maximize customer service levels and optimize operational costs
 + Manage leasing of available space and ensure warehouse facilities are maintained to support shipping and Customer Service

Management of Departmental Financial Responsibilities

* + Create the annual divisional budget
 + Partner with Finance to perform Monthly budget analysis for all Warehouse Operational costs and develop bridge plans to stay within the budget requirements while still maintaining the required Business and Customer service levels
 + Continually identify opportunities for improvement, quality, cost and service
 + Develop Monthly Warehouse Operations Risk & Opportunities based on operational efficiencies/inefficiencies
 + Partner with the Finance team to identify and track the financial impacts of continuous improvement initiatives
 + Ensure that all warehouse operations financial functions are accurate, and timely and meet all established JSOX and financial policies
 + Track, analyze, and report warehouse and 3PL labor costs and develop corrective actions if not achieving targets

Experience & Qualifications:

Education Level

* + Bachelor's Degree (or equivalent experience) in Business, Supply Chain, Logistics or related field- Required
 + Master's Degree (or equivalent experience) Business, Supply Chain, Logistics or related field- preferred

Experience Level

* + Minimum 12 years 
 - Managing a high-volume distribution center including extensive inventory control experience.Managing onsite 3PL vendor relationships and performance metrics.
 + Minimum 10 years 
 - Leading national warehouse operations
 + Minimum 7 years 
 - Continuous Improvement and operational transformation achievements

Software/Technical Skills

* + Warehouse Management System (WMS)
 + Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
 + SAP Order Management

Other Skills/Knowledge/Abilities

* + Strong attention to quality and detail
 + Ability to impact change through influence and collaboration across multiple levels of the organization
 + Ability to successfully manage through complexity
 + Demonstrated leadership and management skills; the ability to motivate positive and cooperative working relationships
 + Knowledge of accounting principles and practices
 + Demonstrated ability to articulate a vision, translating it into executable strategy and driving cross-functional teams to deliver against a plan
 + Advanced continuous improvement skills and operational application
 + Project management and large project oversight experience

 
Additional Details for This Role:

This role will be an onsite role. You are expected to work from the stated job location 5 days a week. #LI-Onsite

Base Salary

* + The targeted base salary range for this position is **$ 165,000.00- $ 185,000.00** per year.
 + Base salary is determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the successful candidate, as well as factors such as internal equity, cost of labor in the hiring location, and alignment with market data.

Additional Compensation

* + This position is eligible for a **30%** bonus at 100% of target, with the opportunity to achieve above 100% dependent on company performance and in alignment with company bonus plans.
 + Bonus awards are discretionary and contingent upon individual performance as well as Brother achieving its corporate objectives, in accordance with the applicable bonus plan in effect.

new_roles.title: Regional Director, Operations
new_roles.description:
Overview:

We are seeking talented, passionate individuals to join our team and help our patients live happier and healthier lives…in their homes.

The Director, Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s home care services. This role provides oversight and direction to branch leadership and is accountable for operational performance, service quality, financial results, regulatory compliance, workforce effectiveness, and growth.

The Director, Operations partners with executive leadership, branch leaders, clinical teams, and other functional departments to drive consistent execution of operational strategies, identify opportunities for improvement, and deliver high-quality, patient-centered care. This role serves as a key leader in developing scalable processes, strengthening branch performance, and supporting the organization’s overall growth objectives.

What We Offer\*:

We know that, to be the best place for our patients, we must be the best place to work for our employees. We offer the 
following to our employees:

* Be part of a unique healthcare company where we can help those in our communities who need our help the

most 

* Flexible hours/work-life balance
* Competitive pay
* Paid on a weekly basis
* Medical/dental/vision/life insurance
* Paid holidays/PTO/401(k) match
* Career growth opportunities
* Great and collaborative work environment

Responsibilities:

What You Will Do:

**Operational Leadership**

* Provide leadership and oversight for the day-to-day operations of assigned home care branches and service areas.
* Lead, coach, and hold branch leaders accountable for operational, financial, clinical, service, and workforce performance.
* Establish and monitor operational goals, performance metrics, and action plans to improve results.
* Standardize processes and workflows across branches to improve efficiency, consistency, service quality, and scalability.
* Identify operational barriers and implement solutions that improve client service, employee effectiveness, and overall performance.
* Partner with other service lines and support functions to ensure effective coordination and execution of organizational initiatives.

**Financial & Business Performance**

* Manage branch budgets and financial performance in partnership with Finance and operational leadership.
* Monitor revenue, labor costs, productivity, staffing levels, utilization, and other key performance indicators.
* Identify opportunities to improve profitability, control costs, and optimize operational resources.
* Analyze performance trends and develop corrective action plans when branches or service areas are not meeting established goals.

**Strategic Planning & Growth**

* Partner with the Vice President, Operations and executive leadership to develop and execute strategic plans for market growth and service expansion.
* Identify opportunities to expand services, strengthen market presence, and improve client access.
* Monitor industry, competitor, regulatory, and market trends and recommend strategies to address emerging opportunities and challenges.
* Evaluate and implement technology, systems, and other tools that improve operational efficiency, communication, and client experience.
* Support organizational growth initiatives, including new market development and mergers and acquisitions as assigned.

**People Leadership**

* Build a high-performing culture focused on accountability, collaboration, service excellence, and employee engagement.
* Recruit, onboard, develop, coach, and evaluate assigned leaders and staff.
* Partner with Human Resources on talent acquisition, employee relations, performance management, retention, workforce planning, and leadership development.
* Establish clear performance expectations and provide ongoing coaching and feedback to direct reports.
* Identify staffing and leadership needs and develop strategies to support workforce stability and growth.

**Quality, Compliance & Risk Management**

* Ensure operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, payer requirements, and organizational policies.
* Partner with Clinical, Compliance, Quality, and other functional leaders to maintain high standards of care and operational compliance.
* Monitor quality indicators, client outcomes, service delivery, and regulatory requirements and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Ensure appropriate policies, procedures, controls, and processes are implemented and consistently followed.
* Support regulatory surveys, audits, investigations, and corrective action plans as required.

**Client & Community Relations**

* Promote a culture of exceptional customer service and patient-centered care.
* Monitor client and family satisfaction and ensure concerns are addressed promptly and appropriately.
* Build and maintain relationships with clients, families, healthcare providers, referral sources, community organizations, and other key stakeholders.
* Represent the organization at community events, industry functions, and other external forums as appropriate.
* Partner with marketing, community relations, and other teams to strengthen referral relationships and market presence.

**Leadership & Collaboration**

* Partner effectively with Finance, Human Resources, Clinical, Compliance, Revenue Cycle, Marketing, and other departments to achieve organizational objectives.
* Communicate operational priorities, performance results, and emerging issues to the Vice President, Operations and executive leadership.
* Promote accountability, continuous improvement, and effective communication across the organization.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

 
Qualifications:

Qualifications:

* Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Nursing, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred.
* Five or more years of progressive healthcare operations or management experience, with demonstrated leadership responsibility.
* Experience managing multi-site, multi-branch, or geographically dispersed healthcare operations preferred.
* Previous home care, home health, personal care, hospice, or other post-acute healthcare experience strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing budgets, financial performance, operational metrics, and performance improvement initiatives.
* Experience leading and developing managers and other operational staff.
* Working knowledge of applicable home care regulations, reimbursement and billing practices, quality standards, and industry trends.

* Eligibility for certain benefits may depend on employment status

CareRing Health is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other classification protected by applicable law.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
**Director of Quality**

Job Type: Full time - Permanent

Location: Bethel, CT📍

A global, private equity backed medical device contract manufacturer is growing fast. With around 20 ISO 13485 certified sites, they make the precision components and sub-assemblies inside many of the world's leading medical devices, from laser-processed nitinol to thin-wall tubing. They're now looking for a Director of Quality to lead product quality and QMS compliance at one of their largest manufacturing sites.

**What you'll do:**

* Own manufacturing quality performance end to end, partnering with Operations to build quality into daily production
* Drive SPC, process capability and data-led problem solving directly on the manufacturing floor
* Lead validation strategy (IQ/OQ/PQ) and quality for New Product Introduction, from development into full-scale production
* Keep the QMS inspection-ready against ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820, and host FDA inspections and ISO audits
* Be the senior quality contact for high-visibility customers and lead the supplier quality program
* Build, mentor and train a quality team in tools like pFMEA, Gage R&R, RCA and CAPA

**What you'll bring:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering or management
* 7+ years in a medical device quality management role
* Hands-on manufacturing quality leadership in an ISO 13485 / 21 CFR 820 environment
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Contract manufacturing, finished device assembly, sterilization oversight, eQMS / ERP and CQA (preferred)
* Willingness to travel around 25%

This is a chance to lead quality at a flagship site within a high-growth medtech manufacturer, with real influence on how quality scales across a global network.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Company Overview**
**Nikkiso Clean Energy & Industrial Gases**
is a leading provider of cryogenic pumps, heat exchangers, process systems, services, and solutions for the LNG and industrial gases industry. We are a subsidiary of Nikkiso Company Ltd, a leading industrial manufacturer headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with over $1.5 B in annual revenue, 8000 + employees worldwide, and publicly traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
 
 
**Nikkiso ACD**
is an engineering and manufacturing company specializing in machinery designed to operate at cryogenic temperatures as low as – 420 degrees Fahrenheit, the boiling point of Liquid hydrogen. For over 50 years, Nikkiso ACD has specialized in centrifugal and reciprocating pumps as well as turbines for air separation. Nikkiso ACD has the most diversified product line in the industry covering nearly every application requiring pumps or turboexpanders.
 
 
**Job Overview**
The Director, Operations is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the manufacturing process. This role will develop and implement strategies that optimize the efficiency and effectiveness of the manufacturing operations to ensure the delivery of high-quality products on time and within budget.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement operational strategies that improve the efficiency, productivity, and profitability of the manufacturing operations for cryogenic pumps
* Ensure that manufacturing operations comply with all relevant safety and environmental regulations
* Develop and manage the annual manufacturing budget and monitor and control expenses to ensure that they remain within budgetary constraints
* Identify and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance product quality while reducing product cost and increase margins
* Manage and develop a large team of manufacturing professionals, providing coaching and mentoring to enable them to reach their full potential
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, and sales, to ensure that products meet customer requirements
* Maintain positive relationships with key stakeholders, including suppliers, customers, and outsourced manufacturing partners
* Develop and implement consistent processes and best practice strategies, policies, procedures, and goals
* Work cross-functionally with product manager, product development, engineering and project management teams to ensure company goals are met and the necessary support to deliver on time is provided
* Lead the effort in identification, recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, training, and ongoing engagement of high-performance team members
* Monitor and analyze key performance indicators for manufacturing such as safety, quality, delivery, cost, cash and, people
* Address escalated customer issues with speed and urgency, orchestrating resources across the company as appropriate
* Identify and remove obstacles to delivering products consistently on time with the right quality

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, or Operations Management, or related field or equivalent work experience
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in a manufacturing leadership role, preferably in the rotating equipment industry
* Extensive knowledge in manufacturing that are consistent with pump products, and how they are manufactured for the cryogenic industry preferred
* Proven track record of developing and implementing operational strategies that improve efficiency, productivity, and profitability
* Experience managing budgets and controlling expenses for operations
* Strong understanding of regulatory requirements and environmental and safety regulations
* Extensive knowledge in lean manufacturing
* Strong knowledge of quality control systems and procedures
* Hands-on experience working with global manufacturing operations
* Broad knowledge of multi-functional and multi-site teams working in a global environment
* Broad knowledge working with cryogenic industries
* Hands-on experience with Problem Solving / Six Sigma
* Project Planning / Project Management experience is preferred
* Ability to communicate effectively with senior management
* Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
* Progressive experience in roles leading manufacturing operations
* High adaptability and flexibility, including the ability to manage deadline pressure, ambiguity, and change
* Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to connect with and positively influence leadership at all levels of the organization
* Self-motivated with extremely strong sense of urgency-act as a change agent in the organization
* Demonstrates excellence in interpersonal skills - verbal and written communication, self-starter, positive make-it-happen attitude, team player
* Able to travel domestically and internationally as needed

**Supervisory Responsibility**
Reports to Director, Operations and manages and develops a team of manufacturing professionals, providing coaching and mentoring to enable them to reach their full potential.
 
 
**Work Environment**
This job operates in both a professional office environment and a manufacturing/production environment. Commitment to safety is essential. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as laptop computers, photocopiers, and smartphones.
 
 
**Physical Demands**
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and ability to adjust focus. This would require the ability to lift files, open filing cabinets and bend or stand on a stool as necessary.
 
 
**Other Duties**
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.
 
 
**Salary Range:**
$150,000 - $200,000 per year.
 
 
**EEOC Statement**
Nikkiso CE&IG is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Director of Manufacturing Operations (low-volume, high-mix or complex assembly req.)**

**Location: East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX**

**Salary: $200,000 - $250,000+ (DOE) + Performance-based Bonus + Benefits**

**Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, Holidays, PTO, Equity Shares**

**Job Type: Full-Time | On-site**

**Typical Hours: Monday-Friday; 40-45 hours/week**

**Start Date: ASAP**

**Sponsorship is not available**

**Relocation assistance available**

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Description**

Our client in the manufacturing industry is looking for a Director of Manufacturing Operations to join their team in East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX. This newly created role will lead approximately 40 employees across production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and continuous improvement, through three direct report managers. You will build the operating systems needed to support continued growth, with an emphasis on improving production flow, standardizing work, strengthening material availability, and reducing order-to-ship lead times. The operation is low-volume, high-mix, and highly customized, making experience applying lean principles in complex manufacturing environments critical. Our client is looking for a manufacturing leader who has led multiple functions and personally delivered measurable improvements from batch production toward flow. This is an opportunity to build and improve an operating system while leading a growing manufacturing organization in a high-demand market.

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Responsibilities**

• Lead production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and facilities

• Develop production flow, capacity, scheduling, and standard work systems

• Reduce order-to-ship lead times and improve on-time delivery

• Build material replenishment, point-of-use, and inventory systems

• Improve supplier performance, sourcing, material availability, and lead times

• Move quality controls upstream to reduce defects reaching final testing

• Establish daily management and structured problem-solving systems

• Lead lean improvements across low-volume, high-mix production

• Develop operations leaders and an approximately 40-person team

• Build capacity to support growth without proportional labor or space increases

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Qualifications**

• 10+ years of manufacturing operations experience required

• 5+ years leading multiple manufacturing departments, including production, required

• Low-volume, high-mix or complex assembly experience required

• Experience leading production flow improvements or measurable lead-time reduction required

• Experience implementing and sustaining lean management practices in manufacturing required

• Experience scaling production capacity or output required

• Manufacturing ERP proficiency required

identity_held_roles.description:
**Sierra Space Careers:**
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.
 
 
Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.
 
 
Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.
 
 
We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.
 
 
**About The Role**
Sierra Space is scaling from development programs into high-rate, repeatable production across a diversified portfolio of military and commercial systems, including satellites and spacecraft, propulsion systems, solar power systems, and the Dream Chaser spaceplane. As Director, Production Operations based in Madison, Wisconsin, you will play a critical role in executing the production strategy for propulsion development and manufacturing, building the operational systems required to deliver hardware at pace, at quality, and at cost.
 
 
This is an execution-focused leadership role for a proven operations professional with expertise in propulsion systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Production, you will lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines and additional enterprise products within Sierra Space's Madison facility. You will drive standardization of production processes, implement data-driven manufacturing systems, and build high-performing teams capable of scaling propulsion output while maintaining quality and efficiency. You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to ensure production readiness and on-time delivery of critical propulsion systems for space and defense applications.
 
 
**About You**
Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.
 
 
We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines, including day-to-day oversight of production floor activities, scheduling, and workflow management at the Madison, WI facility.
* Execute production strategy to scale propulsion manufacturing from development programs into repeatable, high-rate production with a focus on throughput, yield, and cost efficiency.
* Standardize propulsion production processes and workflows to create consistent, repeatable, high-quality build operations aligned with enterprise-wide best practices.
* Support capacity planning and facility buildout efforts for propulsion manufacturing, including layout optimization, equipment installation, and production line commissioning.
* Drive vertical integration initiatives by standing up and maturing internal propulsion manufacturing capabilities, including additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test operations for propulsion components and systems.
* Implement and mature manufacturing execution systems (MES) and production data infrastructure to enable traceability, repeatability, and real-time visibility into propulsion manufacturing performance.
* Establish and maintain production operating rhythm through KPIs, dashboards, and review cadences focused on cycle time, yield, throughput, labor efficiency, on-time delivery, and cost for propulsion production.
* Apply lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies, reduce waste, and improve quality in propulsion operations.
* Collaborate with Propulsion Engineering and Product Assurance to drive design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-test (DFT) into propulsion product development and support new product introduction (NPI) activities.
* Partner across Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness, material availability, and execution against propulsion program schedules.
* Manage production budgets for propulsion operations and analyze manufacturing costs to implement cost-saving measures that maintain quality standards and support financial goals.
* Lead and develop production management teams at the Madison facility, including supervisors, engineers, and technicians, fostering collaboration and accountability while upholding company values and a culture of operational excellence.
* Ensure compliance with industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.) applicable to aerospace and propulsion manufacturing operations.
* Represent propulsion production operations in cross-functional forums and communicate status, risks, and mitigation plans to executive leadership and external stakeholders, including customers and regulatory bodies.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or a related technical field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).
* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, or operations roles in complex technical industries, with a significant portion in leadership positions.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required
* Proven track record of successfully managing large teams and complex production projects in high-rate manufacturing environments.
* Strong background in manufacturing processes, assembly & integration, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems, with emphasis on propulsion systems preferred.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and scaling production operations, including process standardization, workflow optimization, and capacity planning.
* Experience with data-driven manufacturing systems, MES, and production management processes, including OKR development and performance tracking.
* Knowledge of design-for-manufacturing (DFM) principles and ability to collaborate with engineering teams to optimize product designs for production.
* Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and drive operational excellence in fast-paced, highly technical environments.
* Expertise in continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) with proven ability to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies.
* Strong financial acumen with demonstrated ability to manage production budgets, analyze manufacturing costs, and implement cost-saving measures.
* In-depth knowledge of industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.).
* Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to represent production interests effectively to executive leadership and external stakeholders.
* Ability to uphold and model company values while holding others accountable and fostering a culture of operational excellence.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in propulsion manufacturing and test operations, including liquid or hybrid rocket engines, thrusters, or propulsion subsystems.
* Familiarity with additive manufacturing (3D printing) for propulsion components, including metal printing processes and post-processing.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, satellite, launch, or high-rate hardware manufacturing across both military and commercial product lines.
* Experience with vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities such as propulsion, fluid systems, PCBAs, structures, or integrated vehicle production.
* Experience with spacecraft or satellite integration and production.
* Familiarity with classified manufacturing and secure production operations.
* Experience implementing lean or continuous-improvement frameworks at scale in production environments.
* Experience with automated manufacturing, MES implementation, or production data systems.
* Experience leading organizational change initiatives specific to production environments, including technology implementation, process redesign, and workforce development.
* Experience building and scaling production teams during periods of rapid company growth.
* Master's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field.

Compensation:
 
 
Pay Range:
 
 
$164,513.00 - $226,205.00
 
 
Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.
 
 
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:**
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. Citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance.  The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use.
 
 
**Elevate Your Career**
At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations.
 
 
We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more.
 
 
Sierra Space is an industry-leading space and defense technology company providing satellites, spacecraft, and enabling mission systems and components. We deliver mission-proven technologies to our customers that safeguard our nation, protect space-based assets and enable space exploration.
 
 
*Application Deadline: This role will remain posted until a qualified pool of candidates is*
*identified.*
***Please note: Sierra Space does not accept unsolicited resumes from contract agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to our website or to Sierra Space team members not through our approved vendor list or Talent Acquisition will be considered property of Sierra Space, and we will not be obligated to pay any referral fees.***
Sierra Space Corporation is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need special assistance or a reasonable accommodation related to applying for employment with Sierra Space or at any stage of the recruitment process, please contact us.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
identity_held_roles.description:
***Custom Fabrication & Assembly Manufacturing | Southeast Alabama***
**Location:**
Dothan, AL (Onsite).
*Relocation assistance is available.*
**Compensation:**
$165,000 to $180,000 base, plus 10% annual bonus
 
 
**Reports to:**
President, Signage Division
 
 
**Team:**
Top leader on site for a custom manufacturing facility with approximately 125 employees across welding, metal fabrication, CNC, forming, electrical, and assembly
 
 
**Required**

* 7+ years of hands-on manufacturing leadership experience with direct responsibility for plant-level performance, whether as a Director of Manufacturing, Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar role
* Experience leading a labor-intensive, high-mix, low-volume operation such as a job shop, fabrication, or build-to-order environment. Broad manufacturing judgment matters more than deep expertise in any single process
* A track record of improving throughput, labor efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery through steady, practical improvements while keeping production running
* Working knowledge of manufacturing cost, including labor standards, earned hours or standard costing, and how floor performance shows up in a plant P&L
* Strong floor presence and the ability to earn trust with a long-tenured workforce, build real buy-in, and hold people accountable when the reasons for falling short do not add up
* Experience building repeatable systems and a leadership structure that keep a plant running dependably without relying on any one person
* Resourcefulness and comfort delivering results in a lean environment without large corporate engineering or support teams behind you
* Clear, professional communication with executive and finance leadership, including regular reporting on plant performance
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience will be considered
* Genuine comfort relocating to and leading in a small Southern community

**Nice to Have**

* Background in custom fabricated products such as signage, store fixtures, displays, architectural metals, or electrical closures
* Industrial engineering training or a similarly technical, process-focused background
* Experience in a private equity-backed or recently acquired manufacturing business
* Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement experience applied in a practical, hands-on way
* Experience scaling production capacity, including adding shifts or growing output in a constrained labor market

**The Opportunity**
Our client is a private equity-backed national company that designs, builds, and installs branded products for well-known multi-site businesses across North America. This role leads their primary manufacturing facility in Southeast Alabama, a custom, build-to-order operation where a skilled team works hands-on with aluminum, steel, and electrical components, producing a wide variety of products in small lots.
 
 
The plant has made steady progress in recent years, with lower costs, better quality, and more reliable delivery. The next step is a strong, hands-on leader who can keep that momentum going and take the operation further. This is not a turnaround and not a maintenance role. It is a long-term opportunity to increase output, keep improving cost and efficiency, and build an operation that runs dependably every day.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Own plant performance: Lead every aspect of the facility, including safety, quality, throughput, delivery, and cost, with accountability for the plant P&L.
* Lead from the floor: Spend a good part of every day in production, getting to know the people, understanding what drives them, and building the trust that makes change stick.
* Find early wins: In the first 90 days, learn how the factory runs, stabilize performance, and identify practical process changes that make work easier for the people on the floor.
* Drive throughput and cost: Partner with the division President and finance leadership on a multi-year plan to increase output and reduce manufacturing cost, then deliver against it.
* Build repeatable systems: Put processes, metrics, and a leadership structure in place that let the plant run reliably without intensive oversight or dependence on any single person.
* Develop the team: Coach and grow the existing leadership group, including long-tenured leaders who know the product inside and out, and shape the structure the plant needs going forward.
* Hold the line on accountability: Understand the work well enough to see past excuses, set clear expectations, and follow through consistently.

**Why This Role Is Different**
This is the top leadership seat on site. The division President is based in another state, so this person will have real ownership and autonomy over how the plant runs, along with a leadership team that is invested in their success and has done this job before.
 
 
You will not be starting from scratch. The plant has a solid foundation, a clear direction, and the backing of a growing national platform and patient, long-term ownership. The opportunity is to take what has been built and make it better, with room to put your own mark on the operation.
 
 
**The Culture**
The plant has a loyal, tenured workforce that wants to do good work and takes pride in what it builds. The right person brings both process discipline and genuine people skills, someone who can hold the team to a high standard while building the relationships that earn real buy-in. Leadership is not looking for someone to shut things down and start over. They want a steady, visible leader who can find improvements while the work keeps moving, and who will feel at home in a close-knit, small-town Southern community.

identity_held_roles.description:
**About Us**
Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the ha rd work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.
 
 
**Product Development**
From sourcing raw material s to manufacturing, order placement, pricing, quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production/product development team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results-driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.
 
 
**Specific Responsibilities Would Include**
The Director, Sourcing and Product Development reports to the VP of Production for Robert Graham/Saks and will drive seasonal product initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams, including Production, Design, Sales, and Overseas Offices, to develop and execute assigned product lines. The role primarily focuses on apparel development, with additional responsibility for trims and packaging across Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue Private Label.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and manage all aspects of the product development process, from concept and inspiration through quality assurance of finished goods to the end customer.
* Establish shared qualities and fabrics between Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue to ensure alignment across brands.
* Partner closely with overseas hubs and vendor teams to ensure understanding of departmental objectives and leverage vendor capabilities to drive initiatives that expand competencies as needed.
* Analyze product costs, identifying opportunities and collaborating cross-functionally to create solutions through product engineering that maximize product value while accounting for cost impact.
* Oversee cross-functional milestone performance; communicate risks, deadlines, and business impacts when deliverables are at risk.
* Lead vendor sourcing initiatives aligned with driving innovation and service within the overall sourcing strategy.
* Manage new vendor onboarding and ensure all internal partners are connected and prepared to support production needs.
* Facilitate vendor meetings to review in-season development, production, and delivery challenges, and drive solutions.
* Identify business risks and opportunities, escalate appropriately, and propose actionable recommendations for improvement.
* Collaborate closely with Design and Merchandising on product creation from concept to execution, utilizing budget and SKU plans.
* Create and maintain comprehensive material and product libraries with detailed product attributes and testing documentation.

**Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have**

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); advanced Adobe, Photoshop and Illustrator skills required
* SAP experience preferred
* Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills
* Strong team orientation and ability to work cross-functionally
* Ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
* High attention to detail and accuracy
* Knowledge of garment manufacturing, construction, and fabrication

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000
 
 
At Centric Brands, we believe our people are our greatest asset, and we seek to structure competitive compensation offers to ensure that we are able to attract and retain the best talent. Our job postings include an annual base salary range at the time of employment. The stated base salary range represents our good faith estimate as to what candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on several factors, including the selected candidate's educational and professional experience, industry knowledge, location, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the selection process. Base salary is a part of a total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, annual bonus and other Centric Brands sponsored benefit programs.
 
 
**Be part of our growing community by getting involved with groups, teams and initiatives like Be Green, Be Giving, and Be Celebrated.**
**Centric Brands is an Equal Opportunity Employer**
Please note that Centric Brands will only reach out to interview, make an offer of employment or conduct onboarding activities for candidates who have applied through our careers site. When interviewing for a position, the candidate experience will include live interaction, such as a video conference or telephone call, with a Recruiter and/or company employee(s). We will never ask for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process. Be aware of suspicious recruitment activity. If you think you are a victim of an employment scam, you may contact your local law enforcement agency and/or visit the Federal Trade Commission website here: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams .
