existing_roles.description:
**About Varda**
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
**Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.**
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
  
  
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
  
  
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
  
  
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
  
  
**About This Role**
As the
**Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Payloads)**
at Varda, you will own the manufacturing and integration processes for the mission-critical payload systems that define what Varda's reentry capsules actually do in space. Varda's payloads — including pharmaceutical processing hardware, microgravity experiment modules, and government and commercial customer systems — represent the core value proposition of every mission. You will translate payload design requirements into production-ready assembly processes, develop rigorous work instructions, and work hands-on with technicians to ensure payloads are built, integrated, and verified to the highest standards of quality and cleanliness. This role demands both technical breadth and meticulous process discipline: you will interface with external payload customers, internal design teams, and the vehicle integration team to ensure every payload is ready to fly. If you are driven by the idea that what you manufacture will directly enable life-saving pharmaceuticals or cutting-edge scientific research in microgravity, this role is for you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Own end-to-end manufacturing and assembly processes for Varda payload systems, including pharmaceutical processing hardware, experiment modules, and customer-furnished payload equipment
* Develop and maintain detailed work instructions, assembly travelers, process specifications, and acceptance test procedures for payload fabrication and integration operations
* Serve as the primary manufacturing interface for payload customers, translating customer requirements and ICD (Interface Control Document) constraints into executable production processes
* Implement contamination control, cleanliness, and handling protocols appropriate for sensitive payload hardware, including pharmaceutical-grade and precision optical components
* Collaborate with payload design engineers to provide DFM and DFA feedback on assembly accessibility, connector placement, thermal interface design, and testability
* Define and execute payload acceptance testing, functional verification checkouts, and pre-integration inspections; maintain complete and traceable build records
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for payload non-conformances; coordinate MRB dispositions with design engineering and, where applicable, payload customers
* Coordinate payload integration milestones with the vehicle integration team, ensuring payload readiness gates align with overall vehicle build schedule

**Basic Qualifications**

* B.S. in Mechanical, Biomedical Engineering, or a related discipline, with consideration given to equivalent professional experience (typically 6–10+ years)
* 6+ years of experience manufacturing or integrating complex and compact electromechanical assemblies, scientific instruments, or payload systems in aerospace, defense, biomedical, or research environments
* Demonstrated experience building and integrating precision hardware to tight tolerances and exacting cleanliness requirements
* Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, ICDs, and assembly models; familiarity with GD&T and interface requirement management
* Experience developing and executing assembly procedures and acceptance test plans for multi-functional hardware assemblies
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable interfacing directly with customers and cross-functional internal teams
* Must be physically able to regularly lift 25 lbs., bend, stoop, and stand for extended periods while working directly with flight hardware

**Preferred Skills And Experience**

* M.S. degree in Mechanical engineering specialized in Fluid Mechanics, Biomedical Engineering, or related discipline
* Experience manufacturing or integrating spacecraft payloads, scientific instruments, or hosted payload modules for LEO, GEO, or deep space missions
* Familiarity with pharmaceutical or bioprocessing hardware manufacturing requirements, including GMP considerations and contamination control protocols relevant to in-space drug manufacturing
* Background managing payload customer relationships from hardware delivery through integration, verification, and launch readiness
* Experience with ICD management and interface verification processes for payload-to-spacecraft integration
* Knowledge of microgravity experiment hardware design considerations and their manufacturing implications
* Familiarity with environmental testing (thermal vacuum, vibration, shock) as it applies to payload hardware acceptance and qualification
* Experience working in or adjacent to a cleanroom environment (ISO Class 7 or better) for integration of sensitive flight payloads
* Prior work at a company developing commercial space services with a direct end-user product — pharmaceutical, government, or research — where manufacturing quality directly impacted mission outcome

Pay Range
  
  

* Salary Range: $181,913 - $262,763/per year
* This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
* Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
* You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

**Job Description**
The Director PMO NPI/NPD is responsible for leading the successful transition of new products from R&D into scalable volume manufacturing. Sitting within the PMO and reporting to the VP of Production Engineering and Continuous Improvement (PECI), this role owns NPI execution, manufacturing readiness, and phase-gate milestone delivery across the product portfolio. The Director partners closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management to ensure products transition seamlessly into volume manufacturing — meeting customer, quality, cost, and delivery expectations — while building the processes, tooling, and team capabilities needed to scale.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**New Product Development & Launch**

* Own PLM milestone tracking, phase-gate execution, and portfolio pipeline alignment to ensure timely and effective product launches
* Drive product commercialization from R&D handoff through launch, ensuring new products meet or exceed customer, quality, cost, and delivery requirements
* Align cross-functionally on the new product pipeline and launch readiness across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management

**Manufacturing Readiness & Scale-Up**

* Lead the transition of products from R&D into volume manufacturing, establishing scalable and repeatable production processes
* Develop and ramp manufacturing capability and capacity for new products at the R&D site
* Establish and continuously improve the R&D production line to support prototype and pilot builds

**Automation, Tooling & Test**

* Lead automation initiatives including tooling, test fixtures, and production test requirement definition
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to ensure test and tooling solutions are scalable for volume production

**Team Leadership**

* Lead and develop a team of Technical Program Managers and the Engineering Manager for Prototype and Pilot Builds
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement within the NPD PMO function

**Skill & Abilities**
**Ownership & Accountability**
Ability to drive NPI program outcomes from R&D handoff through volume manufacturing launch. Holds themselves and their team to commitments, drives decisions, and escalates risks proactively — ensuring programs stay on track.
  
  
**Program & Portfolio Management**
Ability to manage multiple NPI programs simultaneously across the portfolio, maintaining phase-gate discipline, milestone ownership, and pipeline visibility from commercialization through volume launch.
  
  
**Commercialization & NPI Execution**
Ability to take products through the commercialization phase — from R&D handoff to volume manufacturing — on time and within cost, quality, and delivery targets.
  
  
**Manufacturing & Production Readiness**
Deep understanding of manufacturing processes, scale-up requirements, tooling, automation, and test development — with the ability to translate R&D outputs into production-ready solutions.
  
  
**Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence**
Ability to align and drive execution across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management without direct authority over all stakeholders — critical in a PMO structure.
  
  
**Strategic Thinking & Prioritization**
Ability to manage competing program priorities at the portfolio level, make sound trade-off decisions, and keep initiatives aligned to business objectives.
  
  
**Team Development**
Ability to lead, develop and effectively scale a team to ensure the right capabilities and resourcing are in place at the right time.
  
  
**Stakeholder Communication & Reporting**
Ability to synthesize program status, risks, and decisions into clear, concise communication for senior leadership and the c-suite.
  
  
**Travel**
Ability to travel 10-20%
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical field
* 15+ years of program management experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment, with a focus on new product introduction (NPI), product transitions, or manufacturing scale-up
* 5+ years of team leadership/management role within a PMO, R&D, or Operations function
* Proven experience leading cross-functional initiatives across R&D, Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production readiness, and product commercialization
* Familiarity with PLM systems and phase-gate product development processes

Atlantic Constructors offers competitive benefits, for more information check out our comprehensive list on our website. ACIBuilds.com

**Role Overview:**
==================

The Director of Offsite Production is responsible for the leadership, performance, and continued growth of offsite production across company facilities. The role oversees carbon and stainless steel pipe fabrication and non-volumetric prefabrication and manufacturing, including pipe racks, equipment skids, supports, frames, and multi-trade assemblies. The Director establishes the operating systems, production standards, capacity, and cross-functional coordination required to deliver safe, compliant, high-quality work on schedule.

This leader is accountable for implementing improvements that increase production capacity, labor productivity, throughput, and schedule reliability. The Director will implement and sustain Lean manufacturing methodologies, eliminate waste and production constraints, reduce rework, and create repeatable processes that support scalable offsite manufacturing. The position works closely with Estimating, Engineering, VDC, Procurement, Project Management, Quality, Safety, and field operations to align production with project and business objectives.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**Offsite Production Leadership**
---------------------------------

* Provide enterprise leadership for pipe fabrication, prefabrication, and manufacturing operations across company facilities and approved external production partners.
* Translate backlog, project schedules, and sales forecasts into capacity plans, staffing requirements, production priorities, and facility needs.
* Establish a consistent operating cadence for production planning, readiness reviews, constraint management, performance reporting, and executive escalation.
* Develop scalable operating standards that support growth while maintaining safety, quality, cost control, and predictable delivery performance.
* Coordinate work across facilities to balance demand, available labor, equipment, and production capability.

**Pipe Fabrication Operations**
-------------------------------

* Direct carbon and stainless steel pipe fabrication operations, including material receiving, cutting, beveling, fit-up, welding, inspection, testing, coating coordination, staging, and shipment.
* Ensure spool sequencing, production release, shop loading, and work packaging align with approved drawings, project priorities, and field installation requirements.
* Maintain compliance with applicable codes, specifications, welding procedures, ASME and AWS requirements, customer quality plans, and company standards.
* Improve material traceability, weld documentation, inspection records, testing status, and turnover packages for fabricated systems.

**Prefabrication and Manufacturing Operations**
-----------------------------------------------

* Lead production of non-volumetric prefabricated assemblies, including pipe racks, equipment skids, structural supports, frames, and multi-trade assemblies.
* Develop repeatable production cells, workstations, tooling, fixtures, travelers, and assembly sequences that improve flow and reduce variation.
* Ensure manufacturing plans account for structural, mechanical, electrical, controls, insulation, coatings, testing, preservation, packaging, and logistics requirements, as applicable.
* Support the transition of first-of-a-kind work into stable, repeatable production through lessons learned, standardized design, and controlled process updates.

**Production Planning and Readiness**
-------------------------------------

* Establish production-readiness criteria to confirm approved drawings, bills of material, work instructions, quality requirements, tooling, materials, and labor are available before work is released.
* Partner with Engineering and VDC to improve constructability, spool and assembly breakdown, drawing release sequencing, and design for manufacturing and assembly.
* Coordinate with Procurement and material-control teams to maintain visibility to shortages, supplier commitments, receiving status, kitting, and point-of-use material availability.
* Identify production constraints early, assign recovery actions, and communicate schedule or capacity risks to Project Management and executive leadership.
* Maintain production schedules that clearly identify priorities, dependencies, resource loading, planned output, and required shipment dates.

**Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement**
-------------------------------------------------

* Lead continuous-improvement initiatives that increase production capacity, labor productivity, throughput, and schedule reliability across all offsite operations.
* Implement and sustain Lean manufacturing methodologies, including 5S, standard work, value-stream mapping, visual management, cellular production, daily tiered accountability, Kaizen events, mistake-proofing, and continuous-flow principles.
* Evaluate workflows, facility layouts, material movement, staffing, tooling, and equipment utilization to identify and eliminate bottlenecks, waste, waiting, excess handling, rework, and other non-value-added activity.
* Use time studies, cycle-time analysis, workload balancing, root-cause analysis, and structured problem-solving to improve production performance and reduce manufacturing lead time.
* Develop and maintain standard work instructions and repeatable manufacturing processes that improve safety, quality, training effectiveness, and output predictability.
* Lead initiatives to reduce setup and changeover time, control work in process, improve material flow, and increase productive labor utilization.
* Maintain an improvement pipeline with defined owners, target benefits, implementation dates, and verified results; ensure completed improvements are standardized and sustained.
* Evaluate and implement automation, machinery, software, tooling, and manufacturing technologies that improve safety, quality, efficiency, and capacity.

**Throughput Capacity and Performance Management**
--------------------------------------------------

* Establish production targets and capacity models based on takt time, cycle time, labor availability, equipment constraints, facility limits, and project demand.
* Track and improve key performance indicators such as safety performance, labor hours per spool or assembly, plan attainment, throughput, work in process, first-pass yield, rework, equipment utilization, and on-time completion and shipment.
* Develop visual dashboards and tiered performance reviews that provide timely, accurate information to supervisors, project teams, and executive leadership.
* Analyze performance gaps, determine root causes, implement corrective and preventive actions, and verify that results are sustained.
* Use production data to validate estimating assumptions, workforce plans, capital investments, and future capacity requirements.

**Supplier and External Fabrication Partner Management**
--------------------------------------------------------

* Qualify, onboard, and manage third-party fabrication and manufacturing partners when additional capacity or specialized capability is required.
* Define scopes of work, quality requirements, documentation, inspection points, schedule expectations, material responsibilities, and delivery requirements for outsourced work.
* Monitor supplier performance for safety, quality, responsiveness, cost, schedule adherence, and corrective-action closure.
* Coordinate external production with internal Engineering, Procurement, Quality, Project Management, and logistics teams.

**Estimating and Preconstruction Support**
------------------------------------------

* Support Estimating and Preconstruction with production strategies, labor assumptions, production rates, facility requirements, tooling, equipment, subcontract capacity, and logistics considerations.
* Review proposed scope, drawings, specifications, and schedules to identify production risks, constructability issues, testing requirements, and opportunities for prefabrication or standardization.
* Provide fact-based labor and throughput data to improve estimate accuracy and establish achievable production commitments.
* Participate in make-or-buy decisions and recommend the most effective production approach based on capability, capacity, cost, risk, and schedule.

**Quality Safety and Delivery**
-------------------------------

* Promote a production culture in which safety, quality, and operational discipline are built into the process and are never traded for output.
* Partner with Safety and Quality leaders to establish training, inspections, hold points, audits, nonconformance controls, and corrective-action processes.
* Ensure completed work is inspected, tested, documented, preserved, packaged, and released in accordance with project and company requirements.
* Drive reduction of defects, weld repairs, material damage, punch-list items, field rework, and incomplete turnover documentation.
* Coordinate staging, loading, transportation readiness, and shipment sequencing to support safe handling and efficient field installation.

**Team Leadership and Development**
-----------------------------------

* Build and lead an accountable organization of production managers, superintendents, supervisors, planners, coordinators, and skilled craft professionals.
* Define roles, decision rights, staffing plans, performance expectations, and development paths for the offsite production team.
* Train leaders and production personnel in Lean principles, standard work, problem-solving, root-cause analysis, visual management, and data-driven decision-making.
* Develop succession plans and cross-training programs that increase workforce flexibility and reduce dependency on single points of knowledge.
* Create a culture of ownership, urgency, teamwork, continuous improvement, and respect for people.

**Qualifications and Experience**
=================================

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, manufacturing, operations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Ten or more years of progressive experience in fabrication, prefabrication, manufacturing, construction operations, or a closely related production environment, including significant leadership responsibility.
* Demonstrated success improving production throughput, labor productivity, quality, schedule performance, and operating discipline.
* Practical experience implementing Lean manufacturing or continuous-improvement systems in a production environment.
* Strong understanding of pipe fabrication, welding, structural fabrication, production planning, material control, quality systems, and shop operations.
* Ability to build capacity plans, interpret production data, identify constraints, and translate performance information into corrective action.
* Experience coordinating with Estimating, Engineering, VDC, Procurement, Project Management, Quality, Safety, suppliers, and field teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organizational, financial, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple facilities and competing priorities.

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent formal training in Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement.
* Experience with ASME, AWS, weld-quality programs, fabrication codes, and customer-specific quality requirements.
* Experience with production-planning, ERP, manufacturing execution, scheduling, and performance-dashboard systems.
* Working knowledge of fabrication and detailing platforms such as Stratus, Tekla, SpoolFab, or comparable systems.
* Experience establishing or expanding multi-facility prefabrication and manufacturing operations.
* Experience implementing automation, advanced tooling, production-line design, and capital improvement projects

**Job Summary**

The position of **Plant Manager** is responsible for directing, coordinating, and managing the overall facility operation in conjunction with the customer’s production requirements. Ensure facility production objectives are achieved at the lowest cost consistent with IATF16949 quality requirements. Delegate production leadership responsibilities to achieve the desired objectives set forth in the corporate business plan while maintaining compliance to Federal, State, and Local Safety and Environmental regulations and laws.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Plant Operation
  + Coordinate with the operations manager in the execution of production schedules based on sales requirements and plant capacity.
  + Coordinate and communicate with leadership team and department managers in meeting production goals while focusing on continuous improvement and cost reduction initiatives.
  + Schedule manufacturing activities based on customer releases to minimize inventory.
  + Ensure orders are released in chronological order (FIFO) unless circumstances dictate a change in customer needs.
  + Ensure all “work in process” is properly tagged in accordance with procedures and instructions.
  + Receive and review daily shift reports from leadership team and address areas of concern.
* Ensure the production floor is well equipped, well maintained and efficiently designed
  + Per the IATF16949 requirements, ensure that production floor is equipped with proper work instructions and procedures to carry out production activities.
  + Ensure properly maintained equipment and appropriate trained personnel are available to carry out these activities.
  + Work with operations, program management, and process engineering teams to ensure new programs and process changes are implemented within designated launch plan requirements.
  + Support new program launches and engineer changes that may include floor layouts, staffing, quality and/or tooling requirements.
  + Provide continuous review of departmental processes to improve overall efficiencies.
  + Ensure facility management, making sure the facility meets all production operation requirements.
* Adherence to established policies, processes and procedures
  + Work with leadership team to enforce written policies and procedures to ensure consistency and fairness while maintaining a healthy and safe work environment.
  + Review and approve recommendations of subordinates in matters of position changes and promotions.
  + Work with leadership team to identify and record any issues relating to process failures, policy or procedure violations, or quality system failures
  + When and where required, assist leadership team with attendance management, performance management and corrective action of employees.
* Assist with implementation and compliance of all health, safety, environmental and quality control plans
  + Work with quality department to ensure adherence to the IATF16949 quality standards and corporate quality best practices.
  + Review and disposition of nonconforming products.
  + Assist in providing solutions to prevent reoccurrence.
  + Ensure consistency with implementation and adherence of the company health, safety and environmental policies and processes.
  + Ensure compliance with Federal, State and Local regulatory requirements such as OSHA, EPA, etc.
  + Be visible, assume leadership, and assist in developing and initiating an effective health and safety attitude. Participate and initiate in continuous safety training.

**Qualifications**

* Education
  + Minimum Required: Associates Degree or Technical Accreditation
  + Preferred: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Administration or equivalent
* Experience
  + Minimum Required: 5+ years working in a production environment
  + 2+ years working in a manager or supervisory role in manufacturing/production environment
  + Preferred: 5+ years working in a managerial role in a manufacturing/production environment
* Must have and maintain a valid Driver’s License
* Strong technical background and a general understanding of a manufacturing/production process
* Fluent in English (verbal, reading, writing)
* Must be team-oriented and have excellent communication, organizational and computer literacy skills
* Requires a high level of professionalism and strong work ethic
* Preferred: Familiarity with TS16949 or IATF 16949, Quality Audits, and Environmental Management System and OSHA Requirements

**Working Conditions**

The following working conditions are present or expected on a daily basis:

* Manufacturing/production floor environment with a presence on the production floor required for at least 50% of daily work time.
* Frequent exposure to industrial manufacturing, automotive vehicles, weather elements, chemicals and robotics.
* Personal protective equipment must be worn at all times on the production floor.

**IMPORTANT NOTE**

The organization reserves the right to change, amend or disuse this job description at any time. This document is intended to provide an overview of the required responsibilities and qualifications.

Preferred

* Associates or better

Required

**JOB TITLE: Plant Manager, Dutch Harbor**

**DEPARTMENT: Cesco Solutions**

**REPORTS TO: CCO, Cesco Solutions**

**STATUS: Full time, exempt**

**LOCATION: Dutch Harbor, AK**

**Travel required to Dutch Harbor, approximately 67% of the year in various intervals**

**SALARY: $130,000-$150,000 USD, + Dutch Harbor onsite pay and milestone bonus up to 50% of base salary**

**BENEFITS: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, optional FSA/HSA, 401k with 6% employer match, life and AD&D insurance, Employee Assistance Program, short & long term disability, tuition reimbursement, 8 weeks annual PTO**

**About Us:**

  

**Tidal Vision:**

We believe that sustainability should not require customers to compromise on price, convenience, or performance. Our mission is to create positive and systemic environmental impact by making our biopolymer solutions cost competitive, more convenient, and better performing than the synthetic chemicals we displace. We value innovation and take pride in challenging the status-quo; we choose to view obstacles as opportunities. We value new ideas and encourage the team to apply creativity and invent new solutions to meet challenging demands. We value open, direct communication and foster a collaborative working environment through our unique approach to work culture. We value our employees and demonstrate that through our compensation and benefits programs and opportunities for growth and development.

  

**About Cesco Solutions**:  
Cesco Solutions is the leader in creating client value in liquid/solids industrial water and process applications. Specializing in industries such as food & beverage, paper process and high-organics wastewater overall, we focus on eliminating waste/sludge through reduction and upcycling, at the same time, reducing contamination of downstream biological systems so they run more effectively and efficiently.

As part of Tidal Vision, Cesco leverages chitosan-based chemistry as a sustainable resource recovery approach, to traditional synthetic and metal-based chemistry, to improve paper strength, waste clarification, reduce sludge, and enhance treatment efficiency. By combining advanced chemistry, application expertise, and operational support, Cesco helps facilities optimize wastewater performance, lower chemical consumption, and maintain regulatory compliance while advancing more sustainable treatment practices.

  

**About Tidal Vision’s Unique Work Culture:**

Tidal Vision strives to build and invest in the highest performing and most innovative team. We put our people and customers above process, avoid company-wide rules as much as possible, and have the courage to take unusual approaches to advance our mission. With this approach, we believe we can create a more flexible, fun, stimulating, creative, collaborative, and innovative organization.

**Position Summary:**

We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Plant Manager to lead the operations of our seafood processing facility in Dutch Harbor, AK. This individual will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of plant operations, including production, food safety, quality assurance, maintenance, staffing, inventory management, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a proven leader with experience managing manufacturing or food processing operations, preferably within the seafood, meat, poultry, dairy, or other protein processing industries. This role requires a strong commitment to employee development, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and delivering high-quality products to customers.

**Travel required to Dutch Harbor approximately 67% of the year in various intervals, with Dutch Harbor onsite per day bonus pay. Food and lodging provided.**

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Operations Leadership:**

* Direct and oversee all daily plant operations to ensure production goals, quality standards, and customer commitments are achieved.

* Develop production schedules that maximize throughput, efficiency, and product quality while minimizing downtime and waste.

* Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to safety, productivity, labor efficiency, yield, quality, and on-time delivery.

* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational performance and reduce costs.

* Collaborate with supply chain, procurement, maintenance, quality, and sales teams to ensure seamless operations.

  

**Team Leadership:**

* Lead, coach, and develop hourly production employees.

* Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, employee engagement, and operational excellence.

* Conduct performance evaluations, succession planning, and leadership development activities.

* Recruit, train, and retain a high-performing workforce.

* Promote open communication and maintain positive employee relations.

  

**Food Safety & Quality:**

* Ensure compliance with all food safety and quality standards, including HACCP, FDA, USDA (where applicable), GMPs, SSOPs, and sanitation requirements.

* Support internal and external audits while maintaining regulatory compliance.

* Partner with Quality Assurance to investigate product issues and implement corrective and preventive actions.

* Foster a culture where food safety and product quality are prioritized throughout the organization.

  

**Safety & Compliance:**

* Champion a strong workplace safety culture by ensuring compliance with OSHA regulations and company safety policies.

* Lead safety meetings, incident investigations, and corrective action initiatives.

* Maintain compliance with environmental, health, and safety regulations.

  

**Financial & Operational Performance**

* Develop and manage departmental budgets and operating expenses.

* Monitor labor costs, production yields, inventory levels, and operating efficiencies.

* Identify opportunities to improve profitability through process optimization and waste reduction.

* Prepare operational reports and present plant performance to senior leadership.

  

**Maintenance & Continuous Improvement:**

* Partner with maintenance teams to ensure equipment reliability and minimize downtime.

* Support preventive maintenance programs and capital improvement projects.

* Lead Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, quality, and operational excellence.

  

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Food Science, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; equivalent industry experience will also be considered.

* 7+ years of progressive manufacturing or food processing leadership experience.

* Strong leadership, communication, and employee development skills.

* Experience managing production schedules, labor planning, inventory, and operational budgets.

* Knowledge of food safety regulations, HACCP, GMPs, sanitation programs, and quality systems.

* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience in seafood, seafood processing, aquaculture, meat, poultry, dairy, or other protein processing operations.

* Experience with frozen, fresh, or value-added seafood products.

* Knowledge of seafood handling, cold chain management, and traceability requirements.

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies.

* Bilingual (English/Spanish) is a plus.

  

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to work in refrigerated, wet, and production environments.

* Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the facility.

* Ability to lift up to 50 pounds occasionally.

* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hairnets, gloves, safety glasses, hearing protection, and waterproof gear.

* Willingness to work flexible schedules, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, or holidays as production demands require.

  

**Licensing & Special Requirements**

* Incumbent is subject to a background check.

**Experiencing together a unique human adventure**

Animal health is key to the health of the planet. Working at Virbac means taking part in a unique human adventure in which the engagement of each individual contributes to its evolution. Encouraging internal mobility between positions and countries, offering individual development plans and building a partnership based on trust between managers and employees are as many perspectives of motivation for our teams. We also offer them a work environment conducive to exploring new territories and balancing their professional and personal lives. Finally, fostering their engagement to animal health also means listening to them and helping them to acquire new skills, preparing them for the challenges of tomorrow and encouraging them to contribute to an ever more responsible approach to our business.

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

Virbac Animal Health is seeking a Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology to join our Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) team. The Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology develops, implements, maintains, and improves robust manufacturing processes and facility infrastructure for right-first-time manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs. To plan, schedule, organize, and manage Technology Transfer Projects, CAPEX Engineering Projects, Validation, Technical Support, Alternate Raw Materials, Packaging, Life Cycle Management, and Team Leadership.

**Qualified candidates should possess the following:**

* 8 to 12+ years of Progressively responsible experience in engineering, and production management with a cGMP/FDA-regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Demonstrated track record in CAPEX project management, facility/process design, and multi-team operational leadership across multi-site or regional organizations.
* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.
* Strong multi-team leadership, communication, and cross-functional stakeholder management abilities.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the budget, planning, and robust manufacturing (RFT for the first commercial batches) of technology transfer projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Accountable for the definition and execution of the site and regional project roadmap in alignment with business needs and capability.
* Contributes to the selection of the right technology or CMO, taking into account product needs.
* Establish robust cost estimates (CAPEX, resources, future running costs) and planning estimates to support reliable NPVs and commercial strategy.
* Leadership of scale-up batches, engineering batches, and transfer to production.
* Develops manufacturing documentation (Master Batch Records, Submission batch protocols, etc.).
* Reviews and approves transfer and submission files.

**Expected results:** Ensure the robustness and capability of the process transferred to Manufacturing

**Area of responsibility 2: CAPEX Engineering Projects**

**Main activities:**

* Support and lead CAPEX engineering projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Evaluate, scope, and implement CAPEX projects for facility infrastructure, process improvements, and product needs.
* Responsible for managing annual capital budgets and operating expenses for the department.
* Partner closely with key local and global stakeholders (Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, Finance, etc.) to align project execution with regional operational goals.
* Ensure all engineering projects are performed in full compliance with applicable cGMP standards, EHS regulations, and company sustainability objectives.
* Oversee project budgets, engineering designs, contractor selection, and commissioning/qualification timelines.

**Expected Results:** Successful, on-time, and on-budget delivery of facility, process, and product CAPEX engineering projects that enhance regional capacity, EHS standards, compliance, and efficiency.

**Area of responsibility 3:** Process Improvement & Life Cycle Management (LCM)

**Main Activities:**

* Incorporate structured process improvement concepts (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) across existing product portfolios.
* Lead Life Cycle Management changes to maintain and optimize the existing commercial product portfolio across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Collaborate closely with global and local stakeholders, including Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, and Finance, to evaluate and execute LCM initiatives.

**Expected Results:** Drive continuous product and process enhancement, lower operational costs, ensure ongoing regulatory compliance, and extend product life cycles.

**Area of responsibility 4: Validation**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the generation, technical review, execution, and technical approval of validation deliverables (Validation Master Plan, URS, equipment qualification, process validation, cleaning validation, computer system validation)across NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Lead validation projects and teams
* Ensures risk analysis methods are applied to validation activities
* Follow industry and regulatory trends and expectations (GMP, EHS, and sustainability guidelines).
* Review SOPs and batch documentation to ensure adequacy with validation criteria.
* Ensure prompt deviation resolution, including root cause analysis when required.

**Expected results:** A thorough understanding of the validation status of the regional sites, products, and equipment, with proactive remediation plans addressing any gaps.

**Area of responsibility 5: Technical support.**

**Main activities:**

* Troubleshooting and improvement proposal of current commercial products processes (robustness, productivity, cost efficiency & compliance)
* Lean and methodological approach during trouble shooting of complex product/process deviations
* Take ownership of complex product deviation / CAPA until approval
* Contribute to solution design in collaboration with R&D, Quality Assurance, Regulatory, etc.
* Develop, apply and train teams on efficient troubleshooting and optimization methodologies (FMEA,root cause analysis, etc)

**Expected results:** Deliver strong technical and operational process mastery to support manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.

**Area of responsibility 6: Alternate Raw materials**

**Main activities:**

* Technical feasibility assessments and reporting.
* Leads the engineering or validation batches (protocols/reports)
* Coordinates with the other departments (e.g. Quality Control, Regulatory Affairs)to support raw material changes.

**Expected results:** Support strategic sourcing and continuity of supply through alternate raw material qualifications.

**Area of responsibility 7: Packaging**

**Main activities:**

* Leadership of the packaging change controls and CAPAs (eg: alternate packaging components)
* Collaborates with packaging suppliers on new packaging equipment/materials, and technical feasibility assessments…
* Creates packaging specifications, including drawings and written text areas. Prepares and provides cost estimates for new packaging materials.
* Initiates, leads and Implements packaging improvements for existing products to reduce costs and/or improve packaging and product quality.

**Expected results:** Lead packaging design and modifications to drive productivity, efficiency and cost reductions while maintaining all customer and regulatory requirements.

**Area of responsibility 6: Team Leadership**

**Main Activities:**

* Translate team missions into clear, actionable SMART objectives
* Support and coach team members to help them achieve their full potential.
* Evaluate team performance through key indicators and foster a Lean culture.
* Plan and contribute to the continuous development and training of multi-disciplinary team members.
* Implement standard management practices aligned

with Virbac values while promoting a safe, sustainable working environment.

**Expected results:** Define and implement the NORAM Engineering & MSAT vision and organizational structure in alignment with group strategy.

Joining Virbac means joining dynamic teams ambitious for success.

Location: South San Francisco, CA

Neurona Therapeutics is a clinical stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco focused on the development of neuronal cell-based therapies for intractable neurological diseases.  
We are seeking a Senior Manager, External Manufacturing who will lead our relationships with CMOs/CDMOs and critical suppliers supporting the company’s cell therapy pipeline. This role owns external manufacturing partnerships end to end, from partner selection, onboarding, and technology transfer through campaign execution and ongoing performance management, to ensure reliable, high-quality, and cost-effective manufacturing. The role also supports clinical supply needs by aligning external manufacturing output with clinical program timelines.

The role will partner closely with Technical Operations, Quality, CMC, Procurement, Clinical Operations, and senior leadership to drive strategic partner decisions, resolve risks, and build a scalable external manufacturing network. This is a high-visibility opportunity to shape the external manufacturing strategy of an innovative, growing cell therapy company.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Serve as the primary relationship owner for CMOs/CDMOs and critical suppliers, leading governance forums, joint steering committees, and executive-level engagement.

* Define and track partner performance metrics (delivery, quality, capacity, cost, and responsiveness); lead business reviews and improvement plans.
* Manage external manufacturing schedules, capacity planning, and batch-record and deliverable timelines across partners.
* Partner with Quality and Technical Operations on supplier qualification, audits, changes, deviations, CAPAs, and other GMP-related activities.
* Lead negotiation and management of commercial terms, pricing, change orders, and budgets in collaboration with Procurement and Finance.
* Proactively mitigate risks to partner capacity, critical materials, lead times, and supplier continuity; lead contingency and alternate-source strategies.
* Report on partner performance, risks, and mitigation plans to cross-functional stakeholders and senior leadership; mentor team members as the organization grows.
* Align external manufacturing output with clinical program timelines, working with the clinical supply team on forecasting, inventory planning, and IRT/RTSM needs.

* Cell therapy or advanced therapy experience.
* Experience with supplier qualification, quality agreements, contract negotiations, and change order and budget management.
* Clinical supply chain experience, including forecasting, inventory planning, IRT/RTSM, and GMP packaging oversight.
* Experience in both small biotech (self-driven, requiring problem solving and flexibility) and larger biopharma (more structured training and processes).

--------------------------

Albedo is making Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) mainstream, building the infrastructure to enable every satellite mission to enter this new orbital domain. As part of the first 100 employees at Albedo, you will have a big impact on Albedo's trajectory to proliferating VLEO — whether you're advancing hardware to increase satellite longevity, scaling production for large constellations, building next-gen flight and ground software to push performance, or enabling missions that matter for national security and our day-to-day life here on Earth.

We use AI regularly to create leverage in every discipline across the company. We work in-person at our Broomfield, CO HQ to maximize team and company productivity. We work hard and with urgency to compound our first-mover advantage.

**Who We're Looking For:** Builders who want to own outcomes, not tasks. Systems thinkers who balance precision with iteration while thinking about the big picture. Individuals who are energized by creating a category rather than competing in an existing one. You'll join a team that has already proven what others said wasn't feasible and is now scaling and upgrading our VLEO buses & payloads to serve mission sets across sensing, communications, and responsive operations.

If you can feel the excitement running through your veins, apply to be one of the Bedo 100.

existing_roles.description:
Backed by more than a century of engineering excellence in thermal management technology, Modexus Solutions has sharpened its focus as a specialized leader in commercial HVAC and data center solutions into a new era. Throughout this evolution, our dynamic and collaborative culture, driven by our talented people, has propelled us to the forefront of the industry on a new frontier. At Modexus Solutions, we foster an environment of entrepreneurship and ingenuity, empowering our team to continually drive innovation. Joining Modexus Solutions means unlocking meaningful career growth, continuous development, and high-impact opportunities.

The answer is clear: your next opportunity starts here. Transform the future with us.

For more information about Modexus Solutions, visit www.modexussolutions.com

**Position Description**
------------------------

This role represents a critical executive leadership opportunity for a dynamic Director of Operations – Chillers to join the Global Operations team. Reporting directly to the VP of Global Operations with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President & General Manager (VPGM) of the Chillers business unit, this leader has direct operational responsibility for all global chiller manufacturing plants.

Each global chiller facility holds full SQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) execution accountability. To drive self-sufficient, world-class execution at the plant level, the Director of Operations – Chillers will lead a comprehensive, multi-functional organization where each plant team includes dedicated Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations resources.

As an integral member of the Global Operations team, this individual operates as an influential peer to Supply Chain (partnering to enable global Supply Chain and SIOP execution) and Materials (partnering to enable Materials management and Localized Procurement strategies), as well as the broader Global Operations leadership team. By bridging global functional capabilities with plant-level execution and business unit strategy, the Director of Operations – Chillers will drive rapid operational transformation, capacity expansion, and sustainable business growth.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **1. Global Plant Leadership & SQDC Execution Accountability**

* Hold direct operational oversight and P&L/conversion cost accountability for all global chiller manufacturing facilities.
* Drive rigorousSQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) daily management and execution across every chiller site:

* **Safety:** Champion a zero-injury culture, ensuring proactive EHS compliance, ergonomic improvements, and behavioral safety leadership across all plants.
* **Quality:** Ensure zero-defect manufacturing standards, robust quality management systems, customer compliance, and rapid root-cause corrective actions.
* **Delivery:** Achieve industry-leading on-time delivery (OTD) and lead-time competitiveness through effective line balancing, capacity tracking, and constraint management.
* **Cost:** Optimize direct and indirect labor productivity, overhead absorption, scrap reduction, and continuous conversion cost improvements.

### **2. Multi-Functional Team Management & Talent Development**

* Lead, mentor, and develop Plant Managers and site leadership teams across the global chiller footprint.
* Ensure each plant's respective organization is effectively structured and resourced across Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations to deliver autonomous day-to-day SQDC execution.
* Build organizational capability, establish clear succession plans, and foster an empowered, high-accountability, results-oriented culture across both salaried and direct labor workforces.

**Job Responsibilities Continued**
----------------------------------

**3. Matrixed & Peer Collaboration**

* **Business Unit Alignment (Dotted Line to VPGM of Chillers):** Serve as a strategic operational partner to the VPGM of Chillers, translating commercial growth strategies, customer requirements, and new product introductions (NPI) into scalable manufacturing execution plans.
* **Supply Chain & SIOP Partnership (Peer to Supply Chain):** Collaborate closely with Supply Chain and the Supply Chain/SIOP organization to align long-term capacity planning, master production scheduling, demand-supply balancing, and headcount/capacity models.
* **Materials & Localized Procurement Partnership (Peer to Materials):** Partner closely with Materials and the Materials/Procurement organization to optimize plant-level material flow, inventory turns, working capital, supplier quality/delivery performance, and localized sourcing strategies.
* **Global Operations Synergy:** Collaborate with fellow peers on the Global Operations leadership team to standardize best practices, leverage shared subassembly/hub strategies, and drive enterprise-wide operational initiatives.

### **4. Operational Excellence, Footprint Strategy & Continuous Improvement**

* Define and execute the end-to-end global manufacturing strategy for the Chillers business, aligning footprint optimization, capital investments (CapEx), and automation roadmaps with long-term growth targets.
* Embed Lean manufacturing principles, 80/20 simplification, value-stream mapping, and continuous improvement methodologies across all global chiller sites.
* Support modular design integration, subassembly standardization, and agile manufacturing practices in partnership with Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and Design Engineering.

**Required Education & Qualifications**
---------------------------------------

* **Bachelor’s degree** in Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related technical discipline is required.
* **10+ years** of progressive experience in manufacturing and operations leadership roles (e.g., Plant Manager, Senior Operations Manager, Director of Operations) within complex, engineered-to-order or configure-to-order industrial/HVAC manufacturing environments.
* **5+ years** of proven experience leading multi-site / global manufacturing operations, demonstrating measurable improvements in SQDC metrics.
* Demonstrated success leading cross-functional plant organizations encompassing Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations.
* Deep functional knowledge of Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, 80/20 principles, Sales, Inventory & Operations Planning (SIOP), material replenishment systems, and localized procurement interfaces.
* Proven ability to thrive in a matrixed organizational structure, effectively balancing solid-line functional excellence (to the VP, Global Operations) with dotted-line commercial business unit alignment (to the VPGM of Chillers).
* Exceptional executive presence, communication, and interpersonal influencing skills, with a collaborative approach to working with peer leaders across Supply Chain, Materials, Engineering, and Finance.
* Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally (up to 30%–50% depending on home base location) to support global chiller manufacturing plants.

**Why Choose Modexus Solutions?**

**Health & Well-being:**

* Competitive Health, Dental & Vision Insurance Coverage **on Day One!**
* Additional Benefits After 90 days of Continuous Employment
  + 8 weeks of short term disability leave paid at 100%
  + 4 weeks of paid parental leave paid at 100%
  + Maternity Leave (12 weeks at 100% pay)
  + Paternity Leave (4 weeks at 100% pay)

**Financial Benefits:**

* 401k Retirement plan and company match
* Life Insurance
* Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contribution
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Short Term Disability (company paid)
* Long Term Disability

**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.
* Maintain full compliance with ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and other relevant standards through proactive system management and audit readiness.

**Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving**

* Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for complex production challenges.
* Drive Lean and Six Sigma initiatives that enhance manufacturing efficiency while strengthening compliance and product quality.
* Share best practices across sites to ensure standardization and scalability of quality improvements.

**Customer & Supplier Interface**

* Serve as the primary quality leader for high-visibility customers, ensuring confidence in Resonetics’ ability to deliver consistently high-quality products.
* Lead the supplier quality program, ensuring raw materials and outsourced processes meet stringent requirements to support operational excellence.

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Build and mentor a strong quality team embedded within the manufacturing organization.
* Provide training in advanced quality tools (Gage R&R, SPC, pFMEA, Risk Analysis, Validation, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA) to elevate operational capability.
* Foster a culture of quality culture and ownership on the production floor, engaging all levels of the workforce.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 7 years’ experience in a Medical Device Quality Management role.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Demonstrated background in an ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 quality management system.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and writing)
* BS degree in a management or engineering discipline
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in a technical, regulated environment.
* Experience with finished medical device assembly and oversight of sterilization
* Experience with Quality Management Software (eQMS) and ERP systems
* Certified Quality Auditor

**Physical Demands**

* Light office work, approximately 25%+ travel

**Compensation**
The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000.00 - $222,000.00.
  
  
For temp, temp-to-hire, and regular full-time positions, our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

Saluda Medical is a commercial‑stage medical device company focused on developing treatments for chronic neurological conditions using its novel closed‑loop neuromodulation platform. The company’s proprietary technology senses and measures neural responses to stimulation and automatically adjusts therapy based on real‑time neurophysiological feedback.
  
  
Saluda Medical’s first product, the Evoke® System, is designed to deliver known, consistent, and personalized spinal cord stimulation therapy by objectively measuring neural responses and maintaining therapy within a prescribed therapeutic window. Saluda Medical is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
  
  
At Saluda, we challenge boundaries. We innovate and think beyond the conventional. Our focus is to revolutionize the standard of care in neuromodulation to positively impact patient’s lives.
  
  
The Quality Director reports to the VP QA and is responsible for managing the company’s quality activities at the Bloomington, Minnesota site.
  
  
What You’ll Do:
  
  

* Manage all quality control (QC) activities, to include receiving inspection and product release from the site.
* Manage all quality assurance activities in the distribution facility, to include non-conformance reports (NCR) and supplier quality for our contract manufactured and OEM acquired products.
* Ensure activities performed in the facility are compliant to global regulatory requirements for which we claim compliance, as well as Saluda business expectations.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, be a vocal advocate for a strong culture of quality and compliance at the site.
* Build strong working relationships with other cross-functional leadership at the site to include Supply Chain, Distribution & Customer Service, Clinical, Sustaining Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, ensure products distributed from the facility are handled appropriately and distributed to customers accurately and in a timely manner.
* Provide direct leadership to inspectors, technicians, quality specialists and engineers utilizing an inclusive and empowering leadership approach.
* Manage distribution, contract manufacturing and OEM-related quality challenges as they arise.
* Develop and ensure the implementation of a site inspection readiness plan.
* Participate internal and external audits to ensure the site’s quality system is effective.
* Manage and lead quality improvement projects in all areas of responsibility.
* Organize Supplier Change Assessment Board meetings and ensure submitted change request has the required information for the Change Assessment Board.

What You’ll Bring:
  
  

* Bachelor of Science degree or higher in a life sciences or engineering discipline
* At least 5+ years of experience in medical device quality with 2+ years of leadership experience.
* Proven ability to execute and maintain quality systems, with direct experience in post-market quality, distribution quality, or supplier quality.
* Strong relationship builder and communicator with diverse work teams
* Experience building strong relationships with global colleagues.
* Ability to work on-site 4+ days a week.
* Prior experience with returned product analysis and oversight of U.S.
* FDA 21 CFR Part 806 reporting obligations.

Our Core Values:
  
  

* People – Our first responsibility is to the patients we serve.
* Integrity – Do the right thing
* Pioneering – Lead Boldly, Change Lives, Disrupt the Status-Quo
* Performance – Win together – Deliver with Excellence.

*Saluda Medical embraces diversity and equal opportunity. We are committed to building a team representative of a variety of backgrounds, perspectives and skills. We believe people are the source of our inspiration and innovation.*
*Saluda Medical does not accept non-solicited resumes or candidate submittals from search/recruiting agencies not already on Saluda Medical’s approved agency list. Unsolicited resumes or candidate information submitted to Saluda Medical by search/recruiting agencies not already on Saluda Medical’s approved agency list shall become the property of Saluda Medical.*

For more than 50 years, we have combined scientific rigor with an entrepreneurial mindset, operating with a strong commitment to innovation, accountability, and results to deliver trusted diagnostic solutions.
  
  
As the Diagnostics Specialist, Diasorin continuously invests in research, technology, and people. Guided by our values of operational excellence, customer focus, and teamwork, we empower teams to think boldly, act decisively, and transform ideas into meaningful impact across one of the industry’s broadest specialty diagnostic portfolios.
  
  
When you join Diasorin, you are not just filling a role. You are helping build what comes next.
  
  
**Why Join Diasorin**

* Build What Matters Take ownership, challenge the status quo, and contribute directly to solutions that improve patient care worldwide.
* Innovate with Agility at a Global Scale Work in an entrepreneurial environment that enables speed, collaboration, and global impact.
* Grow in a People-Centered Culture Thrive in a culture that values accountability, inclusion, and continuous development.

**Job Scope:**

Bio-Rad is seeking a Director of Manufacturing to lead our chemical manufacturing operations in Richmond, California, with additional responsibility for developing pilot manufacturing capabilities in Suzhou, China.
  
  
This role provides leadership across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, Quality Control, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety. The Director is accountable for delivering strong performance in safety, quality, customer service, cost, productivity, and inventory while building manufacturing capabilities to support future business growth.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring strong manufacturing and technical leadership, business judgment, and experience leading complex operations in a regulated environment. This position partners closely with Quality, EH&S, R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, and business leadership to ensure reliable operations, successful new product introductions, and a resilient manufacturing network.
  
  
**How You’ll Make An Impact**

* Lead chemical manufacturing operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and customer service.
* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with business requirements, capacity needs, gross margin objectives, and long-term growth.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, QC, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety.
* Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with applicable quality, environmental, health and safety, chemical process safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with EH&S, Quality, Regulatory, Legal, and other functions to proactively identify and mitigate operational, regulatory, and business continuity risks.
* Develop and execute equipment, infrastructure, automation, and capital investment strategies to improve reliability, capacity, and efficiency.
* Drive cost and productivity improvements across labor, yield, scrap, waste, material usage, manufacturing variances, and inventory.
* Partner with R&D and business teams to enable effective new product introduction, scale-up, industrialization, and technology transfer.
* Lead development of pilot manufacturing capabilities in Suzhou to support new product introduction and greater flexibility across the manufacturing network.
* Develop manufacturing budgets and capital plans and ensure disciplined management of operating expenses and investments.
* Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, employee engagement, and development of strong leaders.
* Foster a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and customer focus.

**What You Bring**

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Life Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required; Master’s degree or PhD preferred.
* Work Experience: 12+ years experience leading manufacturing operations in a regulated and technically complex environment, preferably within chemical, life science, diagnostics, pharmaceutical, or related industries.
* Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary manufacturing and technical teams.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing operations, quality systems, EH&S, process safety, and regulatory compliance.
* Strong financial and business acumen, including experience with manufacturing budgets, product costs, productivity, inventory, and capital investment.
* Experience leading operational improvement, capital, automation, capacity, or manufacturing transformation initiatives.
* Experience supporting new product introduction, scale-up, industrialization, and/or technology transfer.
* Demonstrated ability to identify and manage complex operational and business risks while maintaining continuity of supply.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* Demonstrated ability to develop leaders and build high-performing teams.
* Experience working across functions and geographies in a global organization preferred.
* Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, SAP, or comparable manufacturing systems preferred.

**Location:**
This position must be based in
**Richmond, CA**
and requires the employee to be located within commuting distance of the office.
  
  
**Total Rewards Package:**
At Bio-Rad, we’re empowered by our purpose and recognize that our employees are as well. That’s why we offer a competitive and comprehensive Total Rewards Program that provides value, quality, and inclusivity while satisfying the diverse needs of our evolving workforce. Bio-Rad's robust offerings serve to enrich the overall health, wealth, and wellbeing of our employees and their families through the various stages of an employee’s work and life cycle.
  
  
**Benefits:**
We’re proud to offer a variety of options, including competitive medical plans for you and your family, free HSA funds, a new fertility offering with stipend, group life and disability, paid parental leave, 401k plus profit sharing, an employee stock purchase program, a new upgraded and streamlined mental health platform, extensive learning and development opportunities, education benefits, student debt relief program, pet insurance, wellness challenges and support, paid time off, Employee Resource Groups (ERG’s), and more!

The estimated compensation range for this position is posted. Actual compensation will be provided in writing at the time of offer and is based on several factors we believe fairly and accurately impact compensation, including geographic location, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and other job-related factors permitted by law. This position is eligible for a variable bonus, which is dependent upon achievement of your individual objectives and Company performance.

For 70 years, Bio-Rad has focused on advancing the discovery process and transforming the fields of science and healthcare. As one of the top five life science companies, we are a global leader in developing, manufacturing, and marketing a broad range of high-quality research and clinical diagnostic products. We help people everywhere live longer, healthier lives. Bio-Rad offers a unique employee experience with collaborative teams that span the globe. The Director establishes a culture of safety, quality, accountability, inclusion, continuous improvement, and employee development.
